Some say that the movement <term>bhoga</term> of planets through a single constellation <term>nakṣatra</term> consists of 800 minutes of arc <term>kalā</term>—this is the sum total of the planetary and stellar positions. Two constellations plus one-quarter part <note>original: "sapāda-nakṣatra-dvaya"</note> constitutes the movement through one zodiac sign <term>rāśi</term>. Furthermore, within every planetary movement through a sign, there are always nine-fold divisions <term>navāṃśaka; a one-ninth sub-division of a sign, crucial for fine-tuning astrological strength</term>. 25.

Now, regarding the specific movement of the planets: it is said that after determining the portions traversed, starting from the first constellation, Ashvini <note>original: "ashvinito"; the first of the 27 nakshatras in the zodiac</note>, one should calculate the total number of quarters <term>charana; a quarter-part of a constellation, of which there are 108 in the full zodiac</term>. From these, when divided by twelve, the signs are obtained. By dividing the remainder by nine, the planetary positions in the nine-fold divisions <term>navamsha; a 3°20' subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> are found. Again, the purification of these quarters is explained. When the quarters are known, the transit through the signs <term>bhoga; the movement or 'enjoyment' of a zodiacal space</term> is established. 28. Now, he describes the signs in relation to the embodied soul: the sign in which the planet is positioned at birth is fixed. In that sign, the "Jewel of the Day" <note>original: "idunmanih"; a poetic reference to the Sun</note> is said to reside.

---

The portions of the movement through the signs are divided; from these divisions of nine, the nine-fold divisions of the signs arise. Now, beginning from the first constellation, the calculation of the degrees of the planets is called the transit of the sign <term>rashi-bhoga</term>. 28. Regarding the embodied beings: where the Sun is positioned at the moment of birth, that is the birth sign. For the sake of knowing the auspicious time of birth <note>original: "shubha-kala-jetoh"</note> for those whose birth details are unknown, or for a person identified by their well-known name, the following is provided. 30.

---

From that Sun, the Moon is positioned in another place. For the sake of knowing the auspicious time of birth, if the time of birth is known, the calculation is made for that person. From the time of birth, the zodiac sign is determined. For a person whose birth time is not known, the sign is determined from the first letter of their famous name <note>original: "khyata-namantradiko"; referring to the practice of 'Nama Rashi' where the first syllable of a name corresponds to a specific nakshatra quarter</note> and similar indicators. That becomes the person's zodiac sign. 31.

### The Classification of Malefic and Benefic Planets

Now he describes the malefic and benefic planets. **"The cool-rayed one"** <note>original: "shitamshu"; an epithet for the Moon</note> refers to the lord of the cool medicinal herbs <note>In Vedic thought, the Moon is believed to nourish plants and herbs with its cool, dewy light</note>. If joined with these, Mars <note>original: "Mangala"</note>, Saturn <note>original: "Yama" or "Shani"</note>, and the "ray-garlanded" Sun <note>original: "Anshumali" or "Surya"</note> are the "sinful" <term>khala; malefic or cruel</term> planets. Conversely, a strong Moon, Mercury <note>original: "Budha"</note>, Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note>, and Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> are the "gentle" <term>saumya; benefic or mild</term> planets. The signs <term>rashis</term> associated with these planets are also considered by the wise to be gentle or malefic accordingly. 28. Next, he describes the placement of the Sun, its friends, and other factors through their various positions—

> The Sun, known as the ray-garlanded one, and the lord of the cool herbs are always malefic or excellent and good [depending on their strength]. Among those who travel through the sky <note>i.e., the planets</note>, their signs are also remembered by the wise as being either harsh or gentle. 29. These are named and arranged in the wheel. Just as the "five-faced one" <note>original: "panchanana"; an epithet for a lion, referring to its broad or powerful face</note> exists, so it is in the wheel of existence <term>bhava-chakra; here referring to the zodiacal circle</term>. This is protected by the Sun <note>original: "Hari"</note>, who removes the darkness; this house and the others are thus described. 25.

—and he describes the sign Leo <term>Simha Rashi</term> and its lord. The term **"Five-fold"** <note>original: "panchaiti"</note> is used here in a specific sense: just as in the "elephant-faced one" <note>original: "ibha-vaktra"; a reference to Ganesha or elephant symbolism</note> there is a "five-faced" lion, so too in the circle of the zodiac there is a sign called the "Five-faced," which is the sign of Leo. Therefore, the Sun <note>original: "Hari"</note> protects the sign of Leo and dispels darkness. Furthermore, from the perspective of planetary enemies, the Sun alone is the protector; or otherwise, Saturn <note>original: "Shani"</note> is mentioned by the wise in relation to this. In this house, the home of the Lion, it is in hand <note>original: "haste"; perhaps implying "under control" or "in the constellation of Hasta"</note>. 25.

### On the Planetary Lords and the Signs

Regarding the phrase "By the portion of Bhaga" <note>original: "Bhaga"; a Vedic deity often identified with the Sun</note>, it refers to the Sun. In the phrase "removed by twenty" <note>original: "Nakha"; literally "fingernails," a traditional Sanskrit numerical symbol for the number 20</note>, the sign is Leo, and its lord is the Sun <note>original: "Bhaga Surya"</note>. The "Bow" <note>original: "Sharasana"</note> refers to Sagittarius. The "abode in the forest or water" refers to the sign Pisces <note>original: "Meena"</note>, whose lord is Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note>. The "Water-pot" <note>original: "Kalasha"</note> is Aquarius, and the "Sea-monster" <note>original: "Nakra-Makara"</note> is Capricorn; the lord of these two is Saturn <note>original: "Suryatmaja," literally "the Son of the Sun"</note>, who is known by the wise as the "knower of darkness" <note>original: "Timira-vijnah"</note>. This concludes the section on the "vessels" or signs of the planets. This is verse 33.

Furthermore, the signs located at a distance of seven signs from those mentioned are the points of debilitation. What does this mean? For the Sun <note>original: "Surya"</note>, the exaltation sign is Aries; from that sign, the seventh sign, Libra <note>original: "Tauli"</note>, is the debilitation. In this same way:

*   For the **Moon** <note>original: "Soma"</note>, the exaltation is Taurus <note>original: "Go-Vrisha"</note> and the debilitation is Scorpio <note>original: "Vrischika"</note>.
*   For **Mars** <note>original: "Mangala"</note>, the exaltation is Capricorn <note>original: "Mriga-Makara"</note> and the debilitation is Cancer <note>original: "Karka"</note>.
*   For **Mercury** <note>original: "Budha"</note>, the exaltation is Virgo <note>original: "Vala-Kanya"</note>.
*   For **Saturn** <note>original: "Shani"</note>, the exaltation is Libra <note>original: "Tauli"</note> and the debilitation is Aries <note>original: "Mesha"</note>. 34

### On the Exaltation and Debilitation of Rahu and Ketu

Now, the author discusses the absence of exaltation and debilitation for Rahu and Ketu with the phrase "Not conceived." (Verse 35)

### Concerning the Distinct and Identical Nature of Rahu and Ketu

Now, the author discusses the difference and non-difference between Rahu and Ketu with the word "Successively." Those who are masters of sacred sounds <term>Svaravidah; scholars of phonetics or those who interpret the vibrations of the cosmos</term>, as well as those who know the ancient lore <term>Puranas; traditional stories of Hindu deities and history</term>, describe their nature. In the sequence of their manifestation, they are known to the wise as having the "body of a serpent" <note>original: "sarpa-shariram"</note>. Their essence is "composed of darkness" <term>Tamomayam; a substance of shadow or obscurity, as they are not luminous like the Sun or Moon</term>. Indeed, their very form is darkness. 

Regarding the one known as Ketu, it is said in the world that these two were made distinct from one another due to their own actions <note>original: "sva-karmana"</note>. This refers to the "drinking of the nectar of immortality" <note>original: "amritapana"</note>, after which the single body was divided into two parts. Though they are parts of one original body, they are treated as separate. The stories in the scriptures describe how the head was severed from the body, and so on. (Verse 10) 

Now, he speaks of the evidence for their form with the words "Always" and "It is said."

In the context of mathematics <term>Ganita; planetary calculations</term>, their "path" <note>original: "bhakti-gati"</note> and their position—noted in minutes of arc and coordinates <note>original: "kala-adi-rekha"</note>—are always established and visible to the mind's eye. # The Cycle of Planetary Friendships

Now, by means of a poem in the **Vasantatilaka** meter <note>A classical Sanskrit meter of 14 syllables, literally meaning "The Ornament of Spring"</note>, the cycle of friendship among the planets is stated. Regarding the phrase "everything" here, it is said that Saturn and Mercury are the third... <note>The transcription here is slightly fragmented, referring to technical categories of planetary strength</note>. What is explained there? The "Earth-born" <term>Bhauma; Mars</term> is the son of the "All-Bearer" <note>original: "Sarvam-saha," an epithet for the Earth</note>. For the **Sun**, the friends are the **Moon**, the "Teacher" <term>Guru; Jupiter</term>, and **Mars**. His enemies are **Saturn** <term>Surya-ja; the Sun-born</term> and **Venus** <term>Sita; the White One</term>. The remaining planet, **Mercury**, is neutral.

Next, for the **Moon** <term>Vidhu</term>, the friends are the **Sun** and **Mercury**. All other planets are neutral. For the Moon, there is no enemy. (1) Regarding **Mars** <term>Aja; the Ram</term>:

<margin>**Venus** is the [friend] of the **Moon**... these two, **Venus** and the **Sun**, are friends... and **Saturn** (2)</margin>

->The Sun, the Moon, and the Teacher are friends of the Earth-born one;<-
->Mercury is his enemy, while Venus and Saturn are neutral.<-

For **Mars** <term>Kuja</term>, the friends are the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Jupiter**. **Mercury** <term>Ushata</term> is the enemy. **Venus** and **Saturn** are both neutral. For **Mercury** <term>Budha</term>, the friends are the **Sun** and **Venus**. His enemy is the **Moon**. The others—**Mars**, **Jupiter**, and **Saturn**—are neutral.

Next, for **Jupiter** <term>Sura-guru; the Teacher of the Gods</term>, the friends are the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Mars**. The enemies are **Venus** <term>Kavi</term> and **Mercury**. **Saturn** <term>Yama</term> is neutral.

Next, for **Venus** <term>Mrigu</term>, the friends are **Mercury** <term>Somya</term> and **Saturn** <term>Asita; the Dark One</term>. The **Sun** and **Moon** are enemies. **Jupiter** and **Mars** are stated to be neutral.

Next, for **Saturn** <term>Yama</term>, **Jupiter** is neutral... <note>the text ends as it begins to define Saturn's friends, Mercury and Venus</note>.

Now begins the Cycle of Temporary Friendships <term>Tatkalika Maitri-chakra; the temporary alignment of planets based on their current house positions</term> of the planets, as taught by the Sage. Regarding this, the text describes the planets moving along the "Path of the Planets" <note>original: "dvija-vartma-mārga"; literally the path of the twice-born or the celestial path</note>. The Sage states that those located in the nearby Angles and Trines are "Temporary" <term>Tatkalika</term>. These are called "Meeting-People" <term>Sabha-jana; those who honor or join together</term>. Thus, by their mutual positions in the entire circle of the zodiac <term>Rashi-valaya</term>, their status is determined. This is the "Path of the Planets." (52)

These planets are mutually <note>original: "mithah"</note> called "friends" because of this "meeting" <term>sabha-jana</term>. Where? In the entire circle of the zodiac. Because they have sought refuge in one another, those not so placed are called "enemies" <term>abhiyati; those who go against</term>. The term "meeting" is used here to imply a desire for a skillful embrace or connection. As the lexicon <term>Amarakosha</term> states, it refers to the act of honoring or gathering. The distinction between "Supporter" <term>Abhimani</term> and "Enemy" <term>Abhiyati</term> is made clear for the sake of calculation. (52)

### Now, he describes the Ineffective Planet

Now he speaks of the "fruitless" or ineffective planet <term>Viphala-graha; a planet that lacks the power to manifest its results</term>. Even if a celestial body <note>original: "khachara"</note> has reached a favorable position <note>original: "shubha-sthana-gato"</note> in the wheel of houses <term>Bhava-chakra; the basic astrological chart of twelve houses</term>, it may still be ineffective. This occurs when it is not in its own sign <note>original: "na-svago"</note>, or if it has entered its sign of debilitation <note>original: "nīcha-bhavana-gata"; the position where a planet is at its weakest</note>. Furthermore, if it has entered the house of a family of enemies <note>original: "ari-kula-gāh"</note>, its power is diminished. The text mentions the "Sun’s wealth of light" <note>original: "arka-vitta-madi-raktagata"</note>, referring to a planet being combust or overwhelmed by the Sun's rays. This includes influences from Saturn <note>original: "shani"</note>, Mars <note>original: "asṛg-moma/mangala"</note>, and the "Lord of Darkness" <note>original: "timira-rāko," referring to Rahu, the north node of the moon</note>.

-> He who is not in his own sign, who enters an enemy’s house, or whose light is stolen by the Sun, <-
-> Who is mixed with redness or obscured by darkness, though in a good house, <-
-> That planet is ineffective in the wheel of existence; from its location, its strength is gone, <-
-> Even if it dwells within the six divisional charts. (Verse 45) <-

This implies a destruction of power <note>original: "shakti-vināsho"</note>. The "Dark Light" <note>original: "timira-dīpti"</note> refers to the Sun when it obscures others. When a planet is joined with these influences, its speed or "urge" <note>original: "vega"</note> is lost; it becomes "without momentum" <note>original: "vivego" or "vigo"</note>. When it resides in an enemy's house <note>original: "ari-kula-rita"</note>, it becomes a giver of little result, or acts as a malefic planet <term>Pāpa-graha; a "cruel" planet like Mars or Saturn</term>. In this context, even if it is analyzed through the six divisional charts <term>Shat-varga; the six methods of calculating a planet's strength based on subdivisions of the zodiac</term>, such a planet remains "fruitless" or useless <note>original: "niṣphala"</note>. (Verse 45)

### The Twelve Houses of the Horoscope

Now, through this rhythmic meter, the twelve houses <note>original: "dvādasha-bhavana"</note> are described. It is said that the wise <note>original: "vibudhai"</note> have declared the results of the houses in order, beginning from the Ascendant <note>original: "udayā-kramāt"</note>. These houses are named according to the experiences they govern:

1. The House of the Body <term>Tanu-bhava; the first house, representing the physical self and appearance</term>.
2. The House of Wealth <term>Dhana-bhava; the second house, representing assets and speech</term>.
3. The House of Siblings <term>Sahaja-bhava; the third house, representing brothers, sisters, and courage</term>.
4. The House of Happiness <term>Sukha-bhava; the fourth house, representing the mother, home, and contentment</term>.
5. The House of Children <term>Suta-bhava; the fifth house, representing descendants and intelligence</term>.
6. The House of Enemies <term>Ripu-bhava; the sixth house, representing debts, diseases, and opponents</term>.

Now:

-> 1. Body, 2. Wealth, 3. Siblings, 4. Happiness, 5. Children, 6. Enemies, <-
-> 7. Spouse, 8. Death, 9. Religion, 10. Action, 11. Gains, 12. Loss. <-
-> These houses are declared by the wise <-
-> in order from the Ascendant. (Verse 48) <-

Continuing the sequence: the seventh is the House of the Spouse <note>original: "jāyā-bhavane"</note>; the eighth is the House of Death <note>original: "mrityu-bhavane"</note>; the ninth is the House of Piety <note>original: "dharma-bhavane"</note>, often called the "Bull" <note>original: "vrisha"</note>; the tenth is the House of Action <note>original: "karma-bhavane"</note>; the eleventh is the House of Gains <note>original: "āya-bhavane"</note>, where fruits are gathered; and the twelfth is the House of Expenditure <note>original: "vyaya-bhavane"</note>.

### The Results of the Planets

Now, the results of the planets <note>original: "grahanām phalam"</note> are stated. First, the results of the **Sun** <note>original: "ravi-phalam"</note>. When the Sun is in the **ninth house (9)**, the **fifth house (5)**, or the **twelfth house (12)**, its power is <unclear>diminished</unclear>. From the birth sign <term>Janma-rashi; the zodiac sign the Moon occupied at the moment of birth</term>, if the Sun is positioned in the **third (3)**, **eleventh (11)**, or **tenth (10)** <gloss>the house of action</gloss> house, it becomes the bestower of all wealth and success.

Now, the results of the **Moon** <note>original: "chandra-phalam"</note> are stated. The Moon provides prosperity and happiness when it moves through certain positions relative to the birth sign, provided it is not "pierced" or obstructed by other planets.

In the **second house (2)**, or the **twelfth (12)**, or the **fourth (4)**, the intelligence <note>original: "buddhi"</note> or the **fifth (5)** may be affected. In the **ninth (9)**, there is "Bull" <note>original: "Vrisha"; likely a reference to the sign Taurus or a specific strength</note>, but in the **eighth (8)**, there is destruction. If planets are in the **eleventh (11)**, the results are mixed and may be obstructed <term>Vedha; a technical term in Indian astrology where a planet in one house blocks the positive effects of a planet in another house</term>. ### The Results of Mars

Now, the results of **Mars** <note>original: "bhauma-phalam"</note> are stated. If other planets are situated in the **twelfth (12)**, the **ninth (9)** <gloss>the house of penance</gloss>, or the **fifth (5)** <gloss>the house of intelligence</gloss>, then Mars is "pierced" or obstructed <term>Vedha; a phenomenon where the beneficial effect of a transiting planet is blocked by the presence of another planet in a specific house</term>. A person whose Mars is so obstructed becomes one of "afflicted body" <note>original: "viruddha-vapuḥ"</note>.

Mars <note>original: "kuja" or "bhauma"</note> does not grant its full results to the human form in these cases. However, it is generally favorable for siblings, friends, and the acquisition of wealth and the management of disease when positioned in the following houses from the birth sign <term>Janma-rashi; the sign the Moon occupied at birth</term>:

-> The **third house (3)** <gloss>siblings</gloss> <-
-> The **sixth house (6)** <gloss>enemies</gloss> <-
-> The **eleventh house (11)** <gloss>gains</gloss> <-

If Mars is in these positions, it brings results related to wealth and the curing of illness, unless it is obstructed by planets in the houses mentioned before.

### The Results of Mercury

Now, the results of **Mercury** <note>original: "budha-phalam"</note> are stated.

Mercury, known as the "Son of the Moon" <note>original: "vidhu-suta"</note>, acts as a bringer of good fortune <note>original: "shubha-krit"</note> when it transits through the following houses:

-> The **second (2)**, **fifth (5)**, **sixth (6)**, **eighth (8)**, **tenth (10)**, and **eleventh (11)**. <-

It remains auspicious provided it is not "pierced" <note>obstructed</note> by planets located in the corresponding "obstruction" houses. It is said that Mercury is not obstructed <note>original: "na-vidhyate"</note> and remains a bringer of good if planets are **not** in these positions:

-> The **fifth (5)** <gloss>intelligence/mind</gloss> <-
-> The **third (3)** <gloss>valor/effort</gloss> <-
-> The **ninth (9)** <gloss>religion/duty</gloss> <-
-> The **first (1)** <gloss>the body/self</gloss> <-
-> The **eighth (8)** <gloss>death</gloss> <-
-> The **eleventh (11)** <gloss>expenditure/gains</gloss> <-

To clarify the technical terms used for these houses:
The **fifth (5)** refers to intelligence (*mati*).
The **third (3)** refers to valor (*parakrama*).
The **ninth (9)** refers to religion or duty (*dharma*).
The **first (1)** <note>original: "vana"</note> refers to the body or physical self (*sharira*).
The **eighth (8)** refers to death (*mrityu*).

If Mercury, the son of the Moon, is not obstructed by planets in these specific locations, he will be a bestower of good to the person.

### The Results of Ketu

Now, the results of **Ketu** <note>original: "ketu-phala"; the South Node of the Moon, often depicted as a headless dragon or a comet</note> are stated. The wise scholars call him **the Crested One** <note>original: "shikhin"</note>. They say that the nature of the Crested One [Ketu] is similar to that of **Rahu** <note>the North Node</note>. Furthermore, other ancient teachers state that the positions of Rahu are like the forests and the oceans. Measured by fifty-four (54) <note>original: "catuḥ-pañcāśat"</note> degrees or divisions, he moves through the parts of the zodiac. He does not simply travel; rather, when the Crested One [Ketu] rises in the world, he is known by all people to constantly cause great distress.

The wise ones say that when the Crested One is far away, or when he is measured by five "arrows" <note>In Sanskrit poetry, "arrows" (shara) is a numerical code for the number 5</note>, his rising is known to cause suffering to all people in the world. 55

-> By the movement of the enemy's circle [invasion], <-
-> in the night and in the day, <-
-> a state of instability is created. <-
-> The countryside and the people are destroyed by misfortunes, <-
-> and by the loss of their protecting lords. 56 <-

They say he causes pain to the entire world. When he is angry in this position, he stays for fourteen days. When the "Head of the Serpent" [Rahu] comes to the "Feet of the Cold-Rayed One" [the Moon], then the **Wain of Rohini** <term>Rohini-shakata; a specific T-shaped formation in the Taurus constellation. A planet "piercing" this formation was historically viewed as a dire omen of famine or war</term> is "pierced." This occurs by moving in a reverse direction through the <term>Nakshatra; one of the 27 lunar mansions or star clusters used in Indian astronomy</term> until reaching the station of **Punarvasu** <note>The seventh lunar mansion, associated with the stars Castor and Pollux</note>. 57

Now, he prohibits certain actions during the transit of inauspicious planets. In the paths of those who are falling or suffering, on that day and in that transit...

# On the Potency and Qualities of the Planets

Because of the subsistence of **qualities** <term>Guna; the inherent attributes or "colors" of a planet's nature</term>, power is attributed to all the planets. This **power** <term>Shakti; the capacity or potential of a planet to produce an effect</term> is recognized only through the **observed results** <note>original: "drishta-phala-matre"</note>. In that context, the power is conceptualized through numerous qualities, results, or the knowledge of desired fruits. 

Even in the opinion of other teachers, a **conceptual mixing** <note>original: "baudha sankharana"</note> of results is first projected. In this projection, the scope of the power's measure is determined by the qualities. This power is **six-fold** <note>This likely refers to "Shadbala," the six distinct sources of planetary strength used in Vedic astrology</note>, and it attains the very nature of the objects themselves. The bases of these qualities are like a vine; the perceptions of objects are supported by the five-fold collection, just as a group is supported by its own foundation. Because the results are mixed, this distinction of ownership is discarded. A mere example of this is seen in a dream or a festival.

> Power is the essence within the qualities and the results. In the view of the **twice-born** <note>original: "dwijaukasam," referring here to the learned Brahmins or scholars</note>, when a real result is projected, the state of having power is composed of that essence. This is determined through the application of measures.
> In the presence of power, it does not happen otherwise. 55. Qualities bestow excellence upon the actions of objects; the portion of the object is its radiant energy. This should be observed constantly by the wise, even in **human effort** <term>Paurusha; the exercise of free will or personal exertion as opposed to fate</term>. 56.

# On Discernment and the Rituals of Life

Within the **city of qualities** <note>original: "gunave-nagara"; an allegorical reference to the body or the state of being governed by planetary attributes</note>, **discernment** <term>Viveka; the intellectual ability to distinguish between the real and the unreal</term> is considered foremost. This discernment is colored by the wisdom of dharma, and follows the path of the **King of Stars** <note>original: "tara-karaja," referring to the Moon, which governs the mind and emotions in Vedic astrology</note> himself.

In this way, one should consider the potency of a person's life. This consideration begins prior to the **taking of the hand** <term>Panigrahana; the central ritual of a Hindu wedding where the groom takes the bride's hand</term>, and continues through the establishment of the **sacred womb** <note>original: "shri garbha"</note> in an equal state. 

What must be done, and in what manner? One must look to the **ritual of the hair-parting** <term>Simantakarma; a traditional rite of passage performed during pregnancy to ensure the well-being of the mother and the unborn child</term>. This ritual facilitates the state of the "sprinkling" or the **conception ritual** <term>Garbhadhana; the ritual of conception, literally "placing the seed"</term>. Each of these acts is governed by the lords of the planets. It is not something to be done in a hidden or wild place <note>original: "vanya," referring to a forest or uncultivated area</note>.

In the performance of the hair-parting and conception rituals upon the earth, **this means** <note>original: "ityarthah"</note> that one is looking toward the **light of the sun** <note>original: "soraloka"</note>. The completion of these karmic acts is marked here [87]. For those who possess **good offspring** <note>original: "supraja"</note>, the path to the heavenly realm is opened through the city of the body. A devoted wife <term>Pativrata; a woman dedicated to her husband's well-being</term> is like a daughter of the ocean.

After the qualities are established, one looks toward the city. The potency of the Moon (the King of Stars) resides in the "cave" of the hair-parting and the rituals of conception and pregnancy. <unclear>संचोन ते</unclear> <note>The text here is obscured by ink stains, but likely refers to the "joining" or "development" of the embryo</note>. Why is this so? Through the choice of a husband, whatever ritual is performed results in the blessing of **good fortune** <term>Saubhagya; a state of marital bliss, prosperity, and auspiciousness</term>.

Thereafter, following the path of the mother, the sequence continues [18]. In the fourth month of pregnancy, after achieving a state of purity, the child grows. Following this, the beauty of the world is revealed through the arrival of the soul into the family, a numberless and innate excellence. Because of this **good fortune** <note>original: "saubhagya"</note>, one should perform these rituals with a focused mind. The excellence of the woman and the weight of the ritual depend on the "inner city" of her own actions. For this reason, the daughter becomes exceedingly wise. In that state, the fruit of your affection is achieved. This is the truth [18].

# [Folio] 84
## Astrology: Ritual Manual

Then, having risen, the practitioner should consider the light <note>original: "dyotis"</note> and, saying "May we endure," place the thief-like difficulty <note>referring to a spiritual or planetary affliction</note> into a state of resolution. For the sake of protection, after the bathing has been performed with those companions, he then speaks of the **Gorochana** <term>Gorochana: a bright yellow pigment found in the gallbladders of cattle, used for markings and medicine</term>, as well as **Emetic Nuts** <note>original: "madana-phala"</note>. With these substances, what is produced? The purification through the **Five Products of the Cow** <term>Pañcagavya: a sacred mixture of cow's milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung</term>. Furthermore, in the place where the golden essence flows, there should be auspicious **parched rice** <note>original: "laja"</note>. Then he speaks of the mountain-born **mother-of-pearl** <note>original: "shauktika"</note> and **pearls** <note>original: "muktaphale"</note>. Along with these, and along with the moist waters: 83.

Then, with the light of the rising sun, and with the gold, pearls, mother-of-pearl, cow-pigment, honey-fruits, and the five cow-products, it is beneficial for the removal of difficulties.

<margin>
It is said that for the dark-ointment ritual <note>original: "timanjana"</note>, one uses fragrant herbs along with fresh shoots. 84.
</margin>

For humans, this dark-ointment ritual acts as a remover of "thief-like" troubles. 83. One should take **white mustard** <term>Siddhartha: "that which brings success," a name for white mustard seeds used in exorcism and rituals</term>, honey, and the flowers and shoots of the **Malati jasmine** <note>original: "Malati-prasuna"</note>. By these specific lights, the "unevenness" <note>difficult planetary alignments</note> is pacified for the sake of well-being, by which the sorrows of the world are taken away. 84.

The explanation of the white mustard ritual follows: if one is afflicted by the "uneven" or the dark influences, one should use these. In times of crisis or illness, for the well-being of men, the dark-ointment ritual is prescribed. What is the nature of this immersion? It is for those whose birth-circumstances are difficult, for their peace. Therefore, one uses yellow orpiment <note>original: "haritala"</note>, moist roots, and white mustard seeds which are available everywhere. The honey and the well-known **Malati jasmine** blossoms are to be recognized as the primary offerings.

# [Folio] 79
## Astrology: Ritual Manual for the Pacification of Venus

Now he describes the ritual bath for the pacification of the Lord of Venus <term>Shukresha: the planetary deity Shukra, or Venus, who governs beauty, wealth, and semen</term> to prevent destruction <note>original: "nasham iti"</note>. The person, impelled by the "Poet" <note>original: "kavina"; Kavi is a common epithet for the planet Venus</note>, should perform the bathing for the sake of counteracting obstacles. For those who have bathed, he should prepare a mixture with white lotuses, realgar <term>Shilayam: manahshila or realgar, an arsenic mineral used in traditional medicine and alchemy</term>, and fragrant pastes. With these, one should make white water using **lotus stalks** <note>original: "mradalaka"</note> and the fruit of the **Palasha tree** <note>original: "palasha-phala"</note>. At the base of the ritual site, one should chant the mantra: "Do, do, fulfill the desire" <note>original: "kuru kuru kamam ishte"</note>. Regarding the milk and these other substances, some say one should avoid the lotuses and bathe with others instead. 84.

Now he describes the ritual bath for the destruction of calamities <term>Upadrava: sudden spiritual or physical disturbances or "portents"</term>. This involves **Bala** <term>Vala: the herb Sida cordifolia, used for strengthening</term> and the fruit of the **Vela** tree:

-> With the fruits of Vela, Vala, and **Saffron** <note>original: "kumkumaih"</note>, and with white lotuses, <-
-> and with realgar, one should bathe for the sake of <-
-> counteracting the obstacles impelled by Venus. So say some here. 85. <-
-> With Bala and new leaves, with parched rice, <-
-> with clarified butter <term>Ghrita: Ghee</term> flowing from the vessels, and with the Tara-Pranishtha mantras, <-
-> the entire mass of sin is dissolved through this bathing. <-

By the use of these, the darkness of the "dark-faced" one <note>referring to the shadow planet Rahu</note> is dissolved. The performer of the rite attains a state of purity. Why? Because the bath is performed with the power of the white substances. Therefore, for the sake of removing the cause of one's inner agitation, the embodied soul should perform the bathing. For the sake of removing the mass of sins, one uses these ingredients. With what? With **rice** <note>original: "vrihitaih"</note> that has been washed a hundred times. This is spoken of as a cloud-like purifier. With the clarified butter flowing, and with the snakes <note>original: "sarpa"; likely a reference to the Naga-mantras or the nodes of the moon</note>, and with these together, he describes the particular bath that is a hundred times more effective.

## Ritual Baths for Mixed Planetary Conjunctions

Now, in the **Upendravajra** meter <term>Upendravajra: a classical Sanskrit poetic meter characterized by a specific rhythmic gait of eleven syllables</term>, the author describes the pacification bath performed after a transit <note>original: "nistara," referring to the passing of a celestial body through a specific point</term>. The term "Mixed" refers to the overlapping influence of planets. Among the five planets starting with Mars <note>the five non-luminary planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</note>, when there is a conjunction or meeting of two planets, a ritual bath is required. One should bathe using water that has been consecrated with specific materials: **five-colored earth** <note>clays gathered from five different locations, such as a riverbank, an anthill, and a royal palace</note>, **five-colored leaves**, and the **five products of the cow** <term>Panchagavya: a holy purifying mixture of milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung</term>. 51.

->When the influences of two planets are mixed at the time of transit, an anointment should be performed;<-
->Using the five earths, the five sprouts, and the five cow-products. 51.<-

One achieves success and prosperity through immersion with **Shami wood** <note>Prosopis cineraria, a sacred tree used in fire rituals</note>, **Shankhapushpi** <note>a medicinal herb used to calm the mind</note>, **earth from an anthill**, and various flowers. 52.

### General Pacification for All Planets

Now, the author speaks generally of the pacification bath. Immersion at midnight brings about the desired results. With what ingredients? **Shami wood**, **saffron** <gloss>keshari</gloss>, **Padmaka wood** <note>Himalayan cherry wood, used as a substitute for lotus</note>, **Shankhapushpi**, **white mustard** <term>Siddhartha: literally "that which brings success," a common name for white mustard seeds used to ward off evil</term>, and **sandalwood**. With these medicinal herbs, the bath is completed.

# Page 56
## Ritual Libations and the Giving of Gifts

Now, the instructions for the initial libations <term>Tarpana: a ritual of pouring water to "saturate" or satisfy deities, ancestors, or the physical elements</term> are described. He satisfies the vessels of grass <note>likely Kusha grass used in rituals</note> as they are unfolded. He concludes the ritual without neglect. 

**Of what nature is this ritual?** <note>The text uses the traditional Sanskrit commentary style of "Kim-vishishtam" (of what specific quality?) to provide details.</note> 
It involves the offering of clothes. Furthermore, of what kind? It involves the vessel and the lord of the forest <note>Vanaspati, referring to sacred plants</note>. This is the nature of the Varuna-vessel. Furthermore, of what kind? They must be possessing auspicious marks <term>Sulakshana: features that indicate a person or object is spiritually favorable and free from defects</term> and free from any flaws. 

Furthermore, the "Red One" <note>original: "Rohini," here referring to a specific type of cow often gifted in these rituals</note> is mentioned, along with the grains of barley and sesame. These are known as the ritual fees <term>Dakshina: the donation or honorarium given to a priest at the conclusion of a ritual</term> which are highly meritorious. According to the Lexicon <note>original: "Hemah," likely referring to the Hemachandra Lexicon</note>, this brings gold and a pleasant fragrance. 54. 

### The Giving of the Boon-Bestowing Gift

Now, the giving of the boon-bestowing gift <term>Varada-dana: a specific category of ritual donation intended to secure a blessing or "boon" from the recipient or deity</term> is described. It is said to be auspicious. The instructions state: one should offer a red cow <note>Rohini</note> measured with grass, with garments and gold, possessing auspicious marks, and being pure. 55.

The gift of gold or silver <term>Kaladhauta: literally "washed with time," a poetic term for purified gold or silver</term> should be given to a twice-born priest <term>Dvija: "twice-born," a term for a member of the Brahmin, Kshatriya, or Vaishya classes who has undergone the sacred thread ceremony</term>. This gift should be accompanied by the proper ritual fee. This "Red One" (the cow) is the embodiment of the boon. When there is a wise priest, one should give this auspicious gift. 

**Of what quality should it be?** 
It should be together with the "fruit of the remains" <note>Shesha-phala</note>. Furthermore, of what kind? Accompanied by refined gold. Furthermore, of what kind? Accompanied by the red cow. 56.

Furthermore, of what kind? These are the well-known cows offered in the sacrifice, along with white stones <note>possibly referring to specific ritual crystals or ornaments</note>. Furthermore, what is the purpose? To be combined with the ritual fee that exists here. Then, this is for the one who bestows the boon. According to the Lexicon, truth is found in the offspring. In that case, for the priest, the remnants of the vessel are held; the wealth is not to be wasted.

Therefore, the "Red-Eyed One" is indeed auspicious. What are the specific qualities? Red; he is situated in the red prostration. He is understood to be the one who bestows results.

It involves the ritual garment <term>Chivara: traditionally a monk’s robe, but here referring to a specific ritual cloth</term> and a white cloth. What else? It includes fire, wheat, good jaggery <note>unrefined cane sugar</note>, and clarified butter (ghee). This constitutes the planetary circle starting with Mars. 49 

**Now, the ritual gift for Mercury is described.** <note>original: "Atha budha-dānam-āha." In the sign of Taurus, or with a white gift, or born of the feathers of a parrot <note>referring to the green color associated with Mercury</note>. The gift is given to the priests <term>Vipra: a learned Brahmin priest who has mastered the Vedas</term>. The bull is reddish, the son of the Earth is avoided. Having attained that, the wise one is successful. 

With garments that are pleasing and of a preferred color, or indeed of a red-smoke hue, with good jaggery and clarified butter. 50 Regarding the gold, it is possessed of a golden radiance. ### The Ritual Gift for Peace

**Now, the ritual gift for peace is described.** <note>original: "Atha shānti-dānam-āha." This refers to a general ritual to pacify negative influences.</note> When one is afflicted by debt or suffering relative to their birth star <note>original: "janmakhshat"; the nakshatra or lunar mansion the moon was in at birth</note>, or when a planet resides in a difficult position in the birth chart, peace shall be sought. At that time, the ritual of peace should be performed starting with the consecration of a ritual water-pot <term>Kalasha: a ceremonial vessel representing the cosmos or a deity's body</term>. If the "sprouts of pain" appear, what should the ritual include? It requires the "three fruits" <term>Triphala: a traditional combination of Amalaki, Bibhitaki, and Haritaki used for purification</term>. Following this, the peace ritual involves offering fine cloths, iron, and sesame oil <note>original: "taila"</note> to pacify the fires of distress. 10

### The Ritual Gift for Rahu

**Now, the ritual gift for Rahu is described.** <note>original: "Atha rāhū-dānam-āha." By performing this ritual for the shadow planet, which includes the gift of a blanket, iron, and sesame oil, one attains peace. These gifts, particularly when including blue garments <note>blue and black are the traditional colors used to appease Rahu</note>, allow the practitioner to endure and overcome the influence of the shadow planet. <margin>Peace from adversity is brought forth for the one who gives. 20</margin>

### The Ritual Gift for Ketu

**Now, the ritual gift for Ketu is described.** <note>original: "Atha ketūdānamāha." Ketu is the South Node of the Moon, representing the headless body of the celestial serpent and often associated with spiritual liberation or sudden karmic events.</note> For a person who encounters an unfavorable planetary transit <note>original: "viṣama," meaning rough, uneven, or difficult</note> in their birth chart <note>original: "janmavato narasya"</note>, or at times of birth or death, an offering should be made. When Ketu resides in a difficult zodiac sign, one should offer gifts to a twice-born Brahmin <term>Vipra: a learned person, specifically a Brahmin who has undergone the sacred thread ceremony</term>.

What should this gift consist of? It should include **gold** <note>original: "hāṭaka"</note>, **land**, and a ritual fee <term>Dakshina: a traditional gift or honorarium given to a priest for performing a ritual</term>. One should ensure the donation of gold and land when Ketu is in an unfavorable transit. Furthermore, according to the sage **Badarayana** <note>A legendary figure in Indian philosophy, often identified with Vyasa; he is frequently cited as an authority on cosmic laws</note>, a similar gift should be offered when the planet of darkness, **Rahu**, is likewise in an unfavorable position. The sage says that these offerings are vital for those afflicted.

### The Gems to be Worn for the Nine Planets

**Now, the garments and gems to be worn for the Nine Planets are described.** <note>original: "Atha navagraha dhārya māha." The Navagraha are the nine primary celestial influencers in Vedic astrology.</note> **Thus says Hemadri.** <note>original: "iti hemaḥ." Hemadri, also known as Hemadripant, was a 13th-century scholar and minister who wrote influential encyclopedias on Hindu ritual law (Dharmashastra).</note>

For the **Sun**, one should wear **coral** <note>original: "vidruma." While Ruby is more common for the Sun, some regional texts suggest Coral or variants for specific remedial purposes</note>. For **Mars** <note>original: "Bhauma"</note>, one should also use **coral**. For **Mercury** <note>original: "Budha"</note>, the gem is mentioned alongside the "Minister of Indra" <note>Jupiter</note>, for whom one should wear **pearls** <note>original: "mukta-phalam"</note>. For **Venus** <note>original: "Shukra"</note>, specific items are prescribed. For **Saturn** <note>original: "Shani"</note>, one should wear **blue-iron** <note>original: "nīlohaṁ," likely referring to Blue Sapphire or an iron-based remedial ring</note>.

For the other two, **Rahu** and **Ketu**, one should wear **Lapis Lazuli** <term>Rajavarta: a deep blue metamorphic rock used as a substitute for sapphire or for the nodes of the moon</term>. Hemadri notes that even if these are of small size, they possess the power to remove the negative influence <note>original: "vigato mānam"</note>.

If a collapse occurs suddenly in a house, or if a bird enters and falls there, it is an omen. In the case of a golden bird <note>original: "shakuni," likely a specific auspicious or inauspicious bird species interpreted here</note> entering the king's palace, it signifies death. Now, the **Unnatural Phenomena of Birth** <term>Vaikriti: deformities, monstrous births, or biological anomalies considered to be omens</term> are described. Regarding women <note>original: "simantinī," literally 'one with a middle-parting in her hair,' a poetic term for a woman</note>, if a deformity or an unnatural birth occurs—or if a cow produces a deformed calf—it portends disease and danger for the ruler. Likewise, if a mare, an elephantess, a cow, or a buffalo experiences an abnormal delivery, it brings danger to the owner and their entire lineage <note>original: "sa-gotrah," members of the same paternal line</note>. Similarly, if a mare gives birth and the shadow of the newborn appears like a soldier of death <note>original: "kāla-bhaṭopama," resembling the soldiers of Yama, the god of death</note>, it is a sign of great misfortune. Thus says **Hemadri**, noting that such birth defects in women are twice as significant as in animals. If the birth occurs outside the natural time, or if there is an accumulation of sweat or stones, it is a grave sign. (1)

If a mare or an elephantess gives birth to twins, it is a portent of death, like a dark cloud over the village. The results of these events are stated according to the sage **Garga** <note>original: "Gargato," referring to Garga, one of the foundational sages of Indian astrology and omen-reading</note>. (2)

In cases of such "red-eyed" or bloody births, or when one has abandoned their proper duties, one must perform the pacification rituals <term>Shānti: restorative rites intended to neutralize the negative energy of an omen</term> as prescribed by those who desire peace. (3)

Likewise: if at the proper time, one offers food and becomes free from sin, there will be plenty in the city and the danger will subside.

# Regarding the Specific Timing of Births for Mares

Now the nature of births occurring at specific times for **mares** <term>baḍavā: a female horse</term> is described, beginning with the phrase "With the Sun." In the month of **Shravana** <note>original: "Nabhas," the traditional lunar month falling in July–August</note>, "with the sun" refers to the period characterized by the rays of the sun, meaning the birth occurs during the daytime. Specifically, this refers to the end of the month of Shravana, in the fourth fortnight <gloss>or period of time</gloss>. It is explained that they are born in a specific sequence. For the mare, the birth is noted in the first, second, or fourth watch. It further specifies the sun's position in the **zodiac sign of Leo** <note>original: "Siṃha-rāśi"</note> at the time of the birth.

---

-> With the sun, at an auspicious time in the month of Shravana, the mare gives birth, <-
-> producing offspring through careful effort in the proper sequence. <-
-> Again, in the time of the month of Magha, when the sun shines with the beauty of Gauri, <-
-> a dark mare or perhaps a buffalo will bring forth a young one. <-
-> If in the month of Bhadrapada, when the sun is powerful, a birth occurs for the protector of the land, <-
-> it may portend a loss unless specific rites are performed. **Salutation to Rama.** <-

---

When the sun is in this position, the mare gives birth. Furthermore, in the month of **Magha** <note>original: "Tapas," the lunar month falling in January–February</note>, during an auspicious time and on a favorable day, a dark-colored mare or a buffalo gives birth. This timing is specified for the household. In the same way, the birth is noted in the "cold season" <note>original: "hemapaṇe," likely a corruption of Hemanta</note>.

Now, the nature of birth for **female elephants** <term>hastinī</term> in the month of **Bhadrapada** <note>original: "Nabhasya," the lunar month falling in August–September</note> is described. When the sun is in this sign, if a **young elephant** <term>kalabha</term> is born to a female elephant, it is significant. The word *kalabha* refers to the male offspring. In that context, the influence of **Mars** <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: "Yama," often associated with the constraints of Saturn in these contexts</note> is considered, as they may occupy the same house or exert influence on the birth.

<summary>This page details the astrological timing for the births of mares and elephants, specifically focusing on the months of Shravana, Magha, and Bhadrapada as periods of significant omen-reading. The text correlates the sun's position in Leo and the influence of Mars and Saturn with the well-being of the ruler and the state.</summary>
<keywords>astrology, animal husbandry, mares, elephants, Shravana, Magha, Bhadrapada, Leo, Mars, omens, portents</keywords>

# On the Portents Following the Entry into a House

Through these signs, the destruction of the army is predicted. The stolen truth <gloss>or the hidden cause</gloss> is understood through three specific reasons. Now, the results occurring from the time of the **ritual of entering a home** <term>gṛhapraveśa</term> are described. If at the time of house-entry, there is an excess of the "young camel" <note>original: "karabha," likely a reference to a specific astrological shadow or a literal animal sighting</note> or the "enemy of the wolf," it leads to various fruits. Through the influence of **Saturn** <term>Śani</term>, if the master enters a house that is incomplete <gloss>specifically lacking three components</gloss>, then the master of that house will not remain its protector, or he will face a great downfall. How so?

---

-> When in the house, a **horned owl** <term>kauśika</term>, a **jackal** <term>pheru</term>, or other such animals <-
-> wander about in confusion, it portends a loss of flesh and blood. <-
-> If the master of the house is separated from his kin or if his wealth dwindles, <-
-> then it is certain that the prosperity of the master's home is departing. <-
-> If the head of the family becomes excessively fearful, or if <-
-> **new sprouts appear on the wooden pillars** <note>original: "stambha-pravāla-janana"; a classic omen where dead wood coming back to life signifies a reversal of the natural order, usually portending death</note>, <-
-> then it is a sign of a cruel and terrible fate. <-

---

Now, regarding the production of **balls of earth** <note>original: "mṛtpinda," possibly referring to termite mounds or unexplained lumps of clay</note> and other signs, it is said: If in the home of a noble family, an enemy or a person of low character is born, or if balls of earth appear in the house, or if the wooden pillars sprout leaves, these are all signs to be interpreted by those who know the omens. Alternatively, when **birds' nests** <term>vihaṅganīḍa</term> are built in unusual places, or if certain noises are heard, then the master of the family, the owner of the house, will face death, and the family line will come to an end <gloss>literally: "reaches the end of the lineage"</gloss>. Furthermore, regarding the fall of a city: if **jackals** <term>śṛgāla</term> are seen or if they howl near the gates with a terrifying sound, or if a swarm of **ants** <note>original: "pipī [likā]"</note> wanders aimlessly on the ground, then the fall of the city is imminent. How could the protector of the city remain?

# On the Portents of War, Nature, and the State

In the midst of vehicles and men, there is battle <term>saṃgrāma</term>. If the lord is healthy <term>niroga</term> <note>original: "nirogaḥ," meaning free from disease</note>, he remains the master. In a dream, if a bride is seen... for the one born of the subjects...

For a man, when a seat or a throne suddenly shakes or moves in this place, it is a sign of harshness for the man who gives charity...

# Regarding the Omens of Blazing Fire and Water

Now, he describes the remainder of the signs regarding the mass of flames produced from a sudden blaze. It is said that in a **lake** <note>original: "hrada"</note>, such a phenomenon should sometimes be understood to arise from a single source... [unclear] ...the water of a well or similar source. In a **lotus pond** <note>original: "puṣkariṇī"</note> filled with water, if a flame appears and a hand is burned by it, it signifies that the "path of the mind’s journey" <note>this likely refers to the departure of the soul or a loss of mental clarity</note> for men will occur, or there will be a "breaking" <term>bhanga</term> or ruin of the city or its foundations.

Regarding the **portents of water** <term>jalavaikṛta</term>: Just as when a river quickly causes the desolation of a city through the ripening of sins, there are other portents belonging to Varuna <note>Varuna is the ancient Vedic deity who serves as the guardian of the cosmic order and the lord of the waters</note>. In such cases, the waters become turbulent, muddy, and agitated. Even when others approach, he who speaks of this [omen] says it lasts for six months. 2. There may be smoke, or the appearance of flames; the waters may "weep" or behave like sacred grass <note>original: "kuśa"</note> in an unnatural way.

<margin>
In a lake or—this is not specifically mentioned here.
</margin>

-> In a lake or a lotus pond, if fire should ever suddenly arise, <-
-> it portends a journey [death] or a net of various diseases. <-
-> Through such a blaze, one should perceive the burning of the self. <-

Songs, auspicious talk, and the "killing of people" <note>portents of high mortality</note> are indicated by these unnatural water signs. The water may appear like poison or take on the qualities of an ocean. In the event of such a **deformation of water** <term>salilavikāra</term>, which is a form of Varuna, one must perform rituals with the **mantras of Varuna** <note>sacred chants dedicated to the water god to pacify his wrath and restore natural order</note> to find peace. 5. Thus, when such water portents occur, it is believed that the path or way of the people will be affected. If a hand is burned by a flame in the water, it is seen as a sign that a journey from the city <note>perhaps an exodus or death</note> will occur. A blaze that is radiant and intense in a lotus pond, or the appearance of cow dung <note>original: "gomaya"</note> therein, indicates a specific outcome...

# On the Ill Omens of Breaking Water Pots and Other Signs

Now, he describes the misfortune <term>dosha</term> arising from the breaking of water jars and similar objects. Within the home, if a **water jar** <note>original: "udaka-kumbhī"</note> or any vessel used for holding water suddenly breaks, it is a significant sign <note>the text uses "linga" here to mean a diagnostic mark or omen</note>. Whether it is a small **water pitcher** <note>original: "jala-kalaśa"</note> or a large **storage jar**—known as an *ulanjara* in the northern dialect <note>original: "uttara-vedi-bhāṣā"</note>—the breaking of such a vessel indicates that the householder may face death or a great calamity sent by the gods. Furthermore, if a **drinking cup** or another type of tray <note>original: "manya"</note> breaks, it signifies the **loss of life** <note>original: "jīvasya hāni"</note> and the loss of wealth. 12.

Next, he speaks of the misfortunes indicated by pigeons and other birds. A wealthy man <note>original: "bhogi"</note> who is the protector of the house...

-> If in the house, a large storage jar suddenly breaks, it is known to bring the <-
-> fear of death. One attains a loss of life and a loss of wealth through <-
-> the breaking of a drinking vessel or a tray. 13. A wealthy man, seeing <-
-> a pigeon, a crow, or a crane in an unnatural way, or encountering <-
-> a tiger and a boar together, will see the restraint [death] of his city or residence. 13. <-

The term *bhogi* refers to a man of means. A **pigeon** <note>original: "kapota"</note> is the common dove; a **crow** <note>original: "balibhuk," literally "eater of offerings"</note> is well-known as the *kaka*; and the **crane** <note>original: "vaka"</note> is also familiar. When these appear, or when there is an "encounter with a tiger" <note>original: "śārdūla-saṅgama"</note> and an "encounter with a boar" <note>original: "varāha-saṅgama," specifically a wild pig</note> occurring together, it portends a great gathering of ill fate. For that person, it indicates that "the city is restrained," meaning the town or village where he resides will face its end. Alternatively, it means the destruction and dissolution of the village and its dwellings.

Now, he speaks regarding the destruction of the form and other such portents. Regarding the time of the campaign, he speaks of the obstruction by water. If a flowing **river** <term>nadī</term> shows an unusual increase in its waters at the time of the march...

...the abandonment of one's side leads to the loss of the faction. Whether it be a striking blow or the **destruction of the city**, if the pillar is broken, death occurs here for the invader. 18. If a flowing river experiences an unseasonable increase in water, appearing suddenly, it brings **disease to the people** <term>janaruja</term> <note>original: janaruje; literally "people-affliction," referring to an epidemic or widespread sickness.</note> from the states of being. ...or if the water increases unseasonably, why does this happen? If an appearance of danger or calamity occurs in the cities of the enemy, he attains misfortune. Furthermore, if the solar rays are always harsh and a pit which was dug for the sake of lotuses or for the sake of water—having been properly prepared—shows a **whirlpool** <term>āvartā</term> in its middle, then a disease of the people shall occur. A whirlpool is a revolving motion of the water. This refers to a lotus-pond or a reservoir meant for the growth of lotuses.

## The Teachings of Markandeya on Portents

Now, the sage **Markandeya** <note>original: mārkaṇḍeya; a celebrated ancient sage in Hindu mythology, known for his longevity and his presence in the Markandeya Purana</note> speaks regarding the portents that arise. He explains that when these unusual events occur, the King <note>original: rājan</note> or the people encounter the results of their prior **Karma** <term>Karma</term> <note>the law of cause and effect where past actions determine future experiences</note>. Having understood that the experience of these results lasts for a specific period, the wise should perform the necessary propitiatory rites. [98]

The sages <note>original: muni</note> and the noble men have declared that one should not ignore these signs. When natural disturbances appear, a general sense of unease or even the death of the ruler may follow. From where does this stem? It comes from the violation of the natural order and the anger of the gods. One should recognize the difference between the natural and the supernatural. [25] Thus it is said:

---

-> Wherever these wonderful and strange events arise, one must perform the rites of atonement for the actions that initiated them. By observing these signs with logic and reasoning, one should apply the remedy. <-
-> [18] <-

---

Those portents that arise from one's own nature are not necessarily harmful. However, others are considered terrible:
1. **Earthquakes** <term>Mahīkampa</term> <note>literally "earth-trembling"</note>.
2. Strange phenomena during **Twilight** <term>Sandhyā</term>.
3. Sudden **Thunderous crashes** from a clear sky <note>original: nirghāta</note>.
4. Terrible possessions or massive storms of **Dust** <note>original: rajo</note> covering the land.
5. The **Sun appearing red as blood** at both sunrise and sunset. [1]

To the north of these are the omens of **Varuna** <note>the deity of the celestial waters and cosmic order</note>, such as the unexpected appearance of pearls, or an unnatural increase in frost and snow. These are signs for the welfare or ill-fortune of the world. [2]

Furthermore, the falling of **Meteors** <note>original: ulkāpāta</note>, a sky the color of smoke or tawny red, and the sudden bursting of water from dry ground are significant. These are accompanied by unusual sounds from the earth. [3]

When the twilight sky is red as a **Red Lotus** <note>original: raktapadma</note>, it creates a net of defects. When rivers flow backward or in an unnatural manner, these are considered portents of doom for the people of those lands. [4]

<summary>The sage Markandeya lists various environmental portents—including earthquakes, bloody suns, and meteors—that signal the ripening of collective karma and impending national or natural disasters.</summary>
<keywords>Markandeya, Portents (Utpata), Earthquakes, Karma, Varuna, Meteors, Atonement Rites, Twilight Omens</keywords>

Now begins the explanation of the **Pacification of Unnatural Growth** <term>Sanroha Shanti</term> <note>original: saṃroha-śānti; a ritual performed when plants grow in improper places, like inside a house, or when they bloom out of season</note> as received through sacred tradition. On the day a planetary portent <term>Grahotpata</term> occurs, the world can attain peace through the performance of auspicious rites. Whether it is through general offerings or specific rituals, peace is sought for the people. How is this achieved? It is done through the prescribed method of bathing with medicinal herbs <note>original: auṣadhi-snāna</note> and through fire offerings <term>Homa</term>, accompanied by the specific mantras of one's own sacred tradition <note>original: svāgama-bheda-mantraiḥ</note> and the specific mantras of one's own Vedic branch <term>Shakha</term> <note>refers to the specific lineage or "branch" of Vedic study followed by the practitioner's family</note>. [15] 

This is according to the **Aranyaka** <note>original: āraṇyaka; "Forest Treatises," a layer of Vedic text focusing on ritual and philosophy</note>. When portents arise in desolate places, they may not affect the people immediately, but they serve as warnings. Signs include the earth trembling <term>Mahīkampa</term>, strange phenomena during twilight, the sound of thunder in a clear sky <term>Nirghāta</term>, and the appearance of halos <term>Parivesha</term> <note>optical phenomena like sun dogs or lunar halos, often seen as omens</note> around the sun or moon. Other signs include dust storms, smoke, and the appearance of a blood-red sun at sunset. [1] From the trees, we see:

Further signs include the unseasonable appearance of flowers and fruits <note>original: kusuma-phala-udgamāḥ</note>, which signals a disturbance in the natural order. [2] The falling of meteors <term>Ulka</term> causes the sky to appear turbid, bringing distress to the world and the circle of kings. [3] The twilight may appear as red as a red lotus, and the sky may take on the appearance of the moon and sun simultaneously. Such disturbances in the atmosphere and the growth of plants in improper places are caused by the corruption of the elements. In the procedure for conception, the text prohibits two specific types of actions during the lunar junctions <term>Parva</term>. Addressing the "fearful one" <note>original: "bhīro"; a poetic address to the practitioner who is anxious to avoid ritual errors</note>, it states that on the holy days—such as the New Moon and other lunar nodes—the ritual is forbidden. One should understand this specifically regarding the New Moon <note>original: "amāvāsyā"</note> and other such times. The experts in the ancestral rites <note>original: "pitṛ-horā-jña"</note> declare that these times, as well as the "empty" lunar days <term>Riktā</term> <note>the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar fortnight, considered hollow or inauspicious for new beginnings</note>, are causes for failure. [1] One should avoid the time of the Vishti <note>a specific inauspicious astrological period</note> and the "re-married" stars <note>original: "punarbhū"</note>; the reason for this lies in the vow of the ritual. Furthermore, the ritual is prohibited when the Moon is weak and lacking in strength. In the first month of conception, the lord is Venus <note>original: "śukra"</note>; thus, during that time...

---

## On the lunar junctions and other days, O fearful one, the ritual is broken; it is prohibited on the "empty" days <term>Riktā</term> and during the medicinal hours.
## When the Moon is weak, and in the first month... so too the eighth and eleventh lunar days <note>associated with the god Rudra</note>, and the twilight hours—both morning and evening twilight—are avoided by the twice-born.
## The time of midnight <note>original: "kha-madhyamā"</note>, which moves through the middle of the two halves of the night, is condemned in the procedure for the ritual of conception <term>Garbhādhāna</term>. [2]

---

The reason for this is that Venus is the lord of the first month. As it is said in the *Hari-jātaka*: In the first month, the embryo is a "jelly-like mass" <term>Kalala</term> [1]. The lords of the months follow in this order:
1. Venus <note>original: "sita"</note>
2. Mars <note>original: "kuja"</note>
3. Jupiter <note>original: "jīva"</note>
4. The Sun <note>original: "arka"</note>
5. The Moon <note>original: "candra"</note>
6. Saturn <note>original: "kiṃ/śani"</note>
7. Mercury <note>original: "budha"</note>
8. The Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "lagneśa"</note>
9. The Moon
10. The Sun.

These are the respective lords of the gestation periods. Therefore, in the procedure for conception, one must also avoid the eighth lunar day, as it is highly restricted. This knowledge ensures that the child born will not be deprived of vitality. Furthermore, the two twilights—dawn and dusk—are prohibited for the act. Finally, the "middle of the sky" <note>original: "kha-madhyamā"</note> refers to the middle of the night; the text means that the deepest part of the night must be avoided for the ritual. [2]

# Thus ends the first ritual, the Rite of Conception <term>Garbhādhāna-saṃskāra</term>.

Now, [the author] discusses the timing for the rites of Quickening <term>Puṃsavana</term> and Hair-parting <term>Sīmantonnayana</term>. These should be performed according to one’s own caste traditions <note>original: "svajati-dharma"</note> when the embryo has reached the appropriate time. The Quickening ritual is prescribed for the third month or when the fifth month is reached. It is said that the Hair-parting ritual <note>a rite performed to ensure the mental health of the mother and child</note> should also be performed in the fifth month. If it is not performed then, it may be done in the sixth or even the eighth month. 12. Next, he explains the purity of the weekdays <term>vāra-śuddhi</term> for these two rituals: for those desiring a son, these two embryo-sanctifying rituals—the Quickening and the Hair-parting—should be performed by all who wish for success.

---

The husband, following the laws of his own caste, should perform the Quickening and Hair-parting in the third month or when the fifth month has arrived. According to the family lineage <note>original: "svakula-kramāt"</note>, if the time has passed, it may be performed in the sixth or eighth month. For those desiring a son, these two rituals must be done when the planets are favorable, avoiding the *Vibhaṅga* period, the 11th and 12th days, the 3rd, and the 14th day, and the time must be free of the *Pāta* <note>malefic astrological alignments</note>.
->13.<-

---

The lord of the weekday should be Mars <term>Bhauma</term>, the Sun <term>Sūrya</term>, or Jupiter <term>Guru</term>, who is like a minister. These are the six favorable days of the fortnight <note>meaning the male-aligned weekdays and specific lunar phases</note>; these are declared auspicious. What kind of days? Those free from *Vibhaṅga* and the inauspicious *Viṣṭi* <note>a period of time considered cursed for new beginnings</note>. Furthermore, they should be free from the New Moon <term>Amāvāsyā</term>. As Hemachandra <note>a famous scholar/lexicographer</note> says, "the destruction of the moon brings no growth." Additionally, one must avoid the fourteenth day of the lunar cycle, the first day <term>Pratipat</term>, and the malefic alignments known as *Vyatipāta*. 13. Salutations to Rama.

# Now, the Purification of the Ascendant for the Hair-parting Ritual

Now he describes the purification of the Ascendant <term>Lagnashuddhi</term> in the procedure for the Hair-parting ritual <term>Sīmanta-vidhāna</term>. It should be understood that from the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term>, the eighth house is to be avoided, as is the final house <note>the 12th house</note>. Here, the eighth house (8) and the sixth house (6) are to be known as excluded from the Ascendant (12) <note>referring to the three "unfortunate" houses: 6, 8, and 12</note>. With these avoided, the gentle planets <term>Saumya-graha</term> <note>benefics such as Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter</note> should be placed. Furthermore, the 6th, 11th, and 3rd houses from the Ascendant are considered. When the planets are situated in the Trines <term>Trikona</term> (the 9th and 5th houses) or the Angles <term>Kendra</term> (the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses), or when the planet Jupiter <note>Guru</note> is in the 11th house or the 9th house <note>the house of Dharma</note>, the Hair-parting ritual is performed. This is the tradition remembered by the wise. || Thus ends the sacrament of Hair-parting <term>Sīmanta-saṃskāra</term>.

When planets other than the cruel ones <note>malefics</note> are in the houses excluding the 8th and 12th, and when they are in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses; and when the cruel planets <note>malefics</note> are placed in the Trines, the Angles, or the 11th house, and the priest/preceptor <note>representing Jupiter</note> is well-placed, then the Hair-parting ritual is said to be auspicious. 18. Regarding the birth-stars and the days... [there is] no harm in the 12th... in the birth... or in the seventh day... with the name... so it is said. 17. ||

# Now, the Naming Ceremony and the Asterisms

He now speaks of the Naming Ceremony <term>Nāmakaraṇa</term> and the asterisms <term>Nakshatras</term>. Having avoided the "Sharp" <note>original: "Khara"</note>, "Terrible" <note>original: "Ugra"</note>, and "Mixed" <note>original: "Sādhāraṇa"</note> asterisms, and instead choosing the "Fixed" <note>original: "Dhruva," referring to the three Uttara stars and Rohini</note> asterisms; furthermore, during an auspicious rising <term>Udaya</term>, in an auspicious Ascendant <term>Lagna</term>, with planets situated in the Angles <term>Kendra</term> or "Spikes" <note>original: "Kaṇṭaka," another term for the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, and when Venus or Jupiter are present: then the naming should be performed for the boy <term>Bālaka</term>. This is done for the sake of recognition <note>original: "Jñānaka," identifying the person</note> and for worldly dealings <term>Vyavahāra</term>. For instance, one might say, "This child's name is Devadatta." This is performed for the sake of a causal sign <term>Nimitta</term> and for the attainment of a long life <note>original: "Jīvitāya"</note>. Thus, the Birth Rituals are spoken of.

The Sharp, Terrible, and Mixed asterisms are to be avoided for the naming and the act of recognition. When there is an auspicious rising, and planets are in the Angles, and specifically when Jupiter <note>Guru</note> is present, the naming may truly take place. || 18 ||

From the birth month, the lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra</term>, and the day of the week as mentioned, with the strength of the planets <note>original: "Piṇḍa-bala"</note> being favorable, some declare this to be the procedure for naming. Others seek knowledge of the asterism through the two-fold divisions. || 15 ||

# On the Classification of Names and the Selection of the Ascendant

**Now, he speaks of the discrimination regarding names of two syllables and so on.** Drawing from the Brahma <note>original: "Brāhma," likely referring to the Brahma Purana or a similar foundational text</note>, for the first [caste, the Brahmins], and for the second, the **Kshatriyas**, a name of **four syllables** or **two syllables** is prescribed.

<note>Traditional Vedic law codes (Smritis) suggest that a name should have an even number of syllables for a boy and an odd number for a girl. Furthermore, the length often reflected social status.</note>

For the third caste [the Vaishyas] and others, names of **three syllables** are often used. If a name has **two syllables**, it is considered pleasant and powerful. One should avoid names that are too long or difficult to pronounce. These distinctions should be understood according to the specific traditions of one's lineage. || 9 ||

**Now, regarding the purification of the Ascendant <term>Lagna Shuddhi</term> for the naming ceremony:**
The naming should occur during a **fixed ascendant** <note>original: "sthirodaye," referring to the zodiac signs Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability</note>.

---

> Six actions <note>original: "ṣaṭkarma"</note> should be performed. For the four castes, a name of four syllables is auspicious. Or, a name of three syllables, or even two syllables, may be spoken, provided it ends in a vowel and is pleasant to the ear. One should avoid names that are harsh or ill-omened. || 10 ||
>
> In a **fixed ascendant**, or when the sign of the **Bow** <note>original: "Cāpa," the sign Sagittarius</note> or the **Balance** <note>original: "Tulā," the sign Libra</note> is rising, and when the Sun is in a strong position, the name should be pronounced. Specifically, when the planets are favorably placed and the time is free from the gaze of malefic planets, the name is declared. || 11 ||

### The Timing for the Swing Ritual

**Now, he states the lunar mansions and the auspicious moments for the swing ritual.** 

The binding of the swing ritual should be performed with auspicious stars. The stars are: **Swati**, **Ashwini** <note>original: "Trasra"</note>, **Punarvasu** <note>original: "Aditi," the presiding deity of Punarvasu</note>, and **Pushya**. Among these five stars, the ritual for the child is particularly effective. How should they be? Always free from astrological faults.

---

For the installation of the new swing, whether by necessity or on a chosen auspicious day, the binding of the cords should be done when the stars are favorable. 

The installation of the swing is declared to be auspicious in these lunar mansions, provided they are always free from the "strike" of planetary faults. One must especially consider the time of the **Vyatipata** <note>a highly inauspicious astrological alignment or "yoga" that is avoided in all Vedic rituals</note>.

This is the meaning. 

The ritual should be performed when the stars of the Moon and the Sun are in harmony. || 10 ||

### The Auspicious Rocking of the Cradle and the First Outing

The King, whether in a cradle <note>original: "dola"</note> or a palanquin <note>original: "palanaka"</note>, is honored for the sake of joy; thus, he attains his heart's desire. Because of this, rocking the cradle <note>original: "dola-khelana"</note> at an auspicious moment <term>Muhurta: a traditional Indian unit of time, here referring to a specifically calculated "lucky" window</term> is declared to be for the happiness of the King. Some say this ritual is easily accomplished; others say it must be done when the Sun and Mars are favorably placed. One should perform this in a fixed Ascendant <term>Sthira Lagna: an astrological sign that suggests stability, such as Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</term> with benefic planets <term>Saumya Grahas: gentle or positive planets like Jupiter or Venus</term>, having prepared various medicinal herbs and water. The planets should be positioned as follows: in the eleventh house (11), the house of gain; in the first house (1), which is the self; in the sixth house (6); in the tenth house (10), the mid-heaven; or in the "trines," which are the ninth (9) and fifth (5) houses. This should be done when the malefic planets are not in those positions.

---

<margin>The Sun <note>original: "Ravi"</note> and the pride of the King... for the sake of the child... the ritual is performed by those wise in the various ways, in proper order.</margin>

When the cradle is prepared by a person of great effort, the child may attain his desires. The wise ones, who are skilled in the ritual of the first exit, say that when the Sun’s path is clear and four months have passed, the child's desire is fulfilled. This should occur on a day associated with the benefic planets <note>original: "saumya-divasa," such as Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday</note>, or on a day that is generally auspicious.

---
