# On the Timing of the Tonsure Ceremony

Regarding the child’s own clothing and the rules for the cessation of the masculine <note>referring to the transition from infancy or specific gender-based rules for the ritual</note>, should it not be done in a month free of enmity? It should always be performed on an auspicious day. What are the characteristics of this time? It is understood by the wise that the time for the <term>Chaula: the sacred tonsure or first haircutting ceremony</term> occurs when two years have passed, specifically in the third year of the child's life. 28

## Prohibitions regarding Jupiter and Venus

Now, the author discusses the prohibitions regarding the <term>Guru-Shukra-Dosha: an astrological flaw caused by the unfavorable positioning or combustion of Jupiter and Venus</term> during the tonsure ceremony. As stated in the *Shishya-Prabodhini* <note>original: "Shi. Pro."; a classic instructional text for students</note>, the wise do not perform the ritual of the tonsure and other <term>Samskaras: life-cycle sacraments or rites of passage</term> under certain conditions. What are these? When <term>Jupiter: referred to as Guru or the 'Teacher of the Gods'</term> is in an <term>Accelerated motion: 'Atichara,' when a planet moves faster than its average speed through a zodiac sign</term>, or when it is <term>Retrograde: 'Vakra,' the apparent backward motion of a planet</term>, or when it has entered the sign of <term>Leo: Simha-rashi</term>. However, some say there is no opposition from Indra <note>the lord of the gods, often associated with Jupiter's power</note> regarding the tonsure if Jupiter is not currently combust. The rite is forbidden when <term>Venus: referred to as Shukra</term> has set <note>original: "astam gate"; refers to heliacal setting or combustion, where the planet is too close to the sun to be seen</term>. 29

> Having understood the timing for the tonsure—after one year has passed and specifically during the second or third year—one should perform it according to the sequence of rules, in a month that is not hostile and on an auspicious day. 30

As the *Shishya-Prabodhini* states, if a planet is in accelerated motion or if the <term>Ascendant: the rising sign (Lagna)</term> is at the end of a sign, or if both Jupiter and Venus have set, the ritual is obstructed. In such cases, the sequence of the tonsure and other sacraments is not undertaken. 31 

## The Effects of the Months and the First-Born

Regarding the months, it is said that an auspicious ritual should not be performed in a month that causes harm. 40

Now he elaborates on the months and other factors. Regarding the month, it should always be according to the child's birth. As stated in the *Shishya-Prabodhini*, if a month is known to be impure for the family <note>original: "ashaucha"</note>, the performance of the tonsure ceremony will not bring auspicious results. This is especially true for the <term>First-born child: Prathama Santana</term>. For such a child, performing the ritual in the month of <term>Jyeshtha: the 'Elder' month, usually falling in May-June</term> is considered inauspicious and may not fulfill one's desires. This was stated by the scholar Hemadri <note>original: "Hemah"; a 13th-century authority on Hindu law and ritual</note>; it is heard that for the first-born, the ritual in the "Elder" month is to be avoided, as it is only considered excellent for those who come after. 40 ॥

# On the Selection of Constellations for Shaving

Now, regarding the shaving <note>original: "vailena hrapanan," referring to the ritual cutting of hair</note>, the wise who are always proficient in these matters have sent forth the knowledge of the <term>Horas: astrological hours or time-divisions</term> and the constellations. They say that the "movable" constellations are to be used. These are understood by the experts to be: <term>Punarvasu: the seventh lunar mansion, 'the two restorers of goods'</term>, <term>Ashvini: the first lunar mansion, 'the horse-headed twins'</term>, <term>Hasta: the thirteenth lunar mansion, 'the hand'</term>, <term>Chitra: the fourteenth lunar mansion, 'the bright one'</term>, and <term>Revati: the twenty-seventh lunar mansion, 'the wealthy'</term>.

These <term>Nakshatras: lunar mansions</term>, specifically Chitra and Revati, are known by the astrologers to be auspicious when they are within the influence of a <term>Benefic: 'Saumya,' planets like Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter that grant favorable results</term>. 40

## Prohibitions of Specific Lunar Days

Next, the author prohibits certain times. He speaks of the <term>Sandhi: the 'junctions' or transition points between two lunar days or signs</term>. The lunar days that are "colored" or affected by these junctions are considered spoiled and are rejected in the <term>Kandharaka: a specific astrological calculation or manual</term>. These lunar days are avoided because they are "possessed" by unfavorable spirits <note>referring to the 'Yogi' or 'Bhuta' influences that make a time spiritually unstable</note>.

The "movable" constellations mentioned before are favored by the experts, but they must be <insert>Avoided <br/> [in the following] <br/> [cases] <br/> 4 <br/> 1</insert> <note>original insert: "Varjitah 41"</note> when the astrological hours are not in a favorable interval. 41

### Specifically Prohibited Lunar Days and Times

Furthermore, what else is excluded? The following <term>Tithis: lunar days</term> are avoided: the <term>Shasthi: the 6th day of the lunar fortnight</term>, the <term>Amavasya: the New Moon day</term>, the <term>Ashtami: the 8th day of the lunar fortnight</term>, and the <term>Purnima: the Full Moon day</term>. These are the lunar days 6, 30 <note>Amavasya</note>, 8, and 15 <note>Purnima</note>. 

Additionally, one must avoid the <term>Bhadra Karana: an inauspicious astrological period often personified as a goddess to be appeased or avoided</term>. 41

Now, regarding the <term>Gochara: the current transit of planets through the zodiac</term>. Even if a constellation is generally good, the expert astrologer must check the current positions. The ceremony should not be performed if the transit is unfavorable for the child's birth star. 

Finally, one must never perform the ritual during the <term>Sandhya: the morning or evening twilight</term>, nor at night. One must wait for a time that is free from the <term>Bhadra: the 'inauspicious' time division</term>. 42

### Now, the Rules for the Initiation Ritual

Following the description of worldly customs, the instructions for the **initiation ritual** <term>Upanayana: the sacred thread ceremony marking the start of a student's formal education</term> are provided. Scholars who know the laws of the Vedas <note>original: "śrutidharmavido"</note> have determined that the timing should be calculated either from birth or from **conception** <term>Garbhadhana: the first of the life-cycle rituals, performed at the time of conception</term>. In the eighth year, or even in the fifth year, the **tying of the girdle** <term>Mauñjībandhana: another name for Upanayana, referring to the grass belt worn by the student</term> is to be performed for the sons of the twice-born <term>Dvija: 'twice-born' or the three highest social classes—Brahmana, Kshatriya, and Vaishya</term>. Specifically for **Brahmanas** <note>the priestly or scholarly class</note>, the sage Kashyapa spoke these words, emphasizing that this is for the purpose of attaining higher knowledge. <gloss>From birth or from successful conception: the knowers of the Vedic laws understand the proper timing. Some authorities state the ritual may occur as early as the 5th year. Some suggest other intervals <note>original: "kāścit"</note> depending on the family tradition.</gloss>

For the **Kshatriyas** <note>the warrior and ruling class</note>, the ritual involves the tying of a bowstring; for the **Vaishyas** <note>the merchant and agricultural class</note>, it involves a hempen or woolly thread, according to the specific scriptures.

Now, the instruction regarding the stages of life <note>original: "āśrama"</note> follows. ### The Consensus of the <unclear>Sages</unclear> on the Timing of Vows

Regarding the timing of the vow <term>Vratavedha: the precise moment when a sacred vow or initiation begins</term>, the author describes the tradition of the wise. It is said that by observing the positions of the planets—specifically Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note>—the learned ones who understand the celestial realms have determined the proper timing. For the Vaishyas <note>the merchant and agricultural class</note>, the seventh year is praised by those who follow the ancient methods. This has been declared by the gods and the sages of perfect intellect as the standard for these years. 5

### The Timing of Vows during the Northern Solstice

<margin>The direction of the solstice</margin>

### Rules Regarding the Affliction of Jupiter 

Now, the author establishes the rules for the initiation vow when there is a flaw <term>Dosha: a blemish or unfavorable astrological alignment</term> concerning Jupiter. The initiation should not take place if Jupiter is positioned in certain ways. If the planet is in its own exaltation <note>original: "Tunga," the point where a planet's influence is strongest</note> or in the seventh house, or if it is retrograde, or if the celestial body is afflicted, the ancient texts advise caution. For the sake of all the gods and the lineage of the sages, one must ensure the heavens are clear of these specific flaws before the child begins the vow.

# Prohibitions of Rituals during the Infancy and Old Age of Venus and the Moon

Now, the text prohibits the performance of vows during the "old age" or "infancy" of Venus and the Moon. The term "Child of Diti" <note>original: "Ditija-guru," referring to Venus as the preceptor of the Daityas or Titans</note> refers to Venus, and the "Lord of Night" <note>original: "Nisheesha"</note> refers to the Moon. When these two are in their states of old age or infancy <term>Vriddha-Balatva: astronomical states where a planet is either too close to the Sun (combust) or has just emerged and lacks "strength"</term>, the traditional scriptures <note>original: "Nigama"</note> state that the initiation ceremony <term>Upavita: the investiture of the sacred thread</term> for a boy—specifically one around eight years of age—should not be performed. The purpose of this rule is to prevent the loss of the spiritual merit derived from the Vedic teachings. 8

Furthermore, the text prohibits the binding of the vow during earthquakes and similar omens. The wise understand that from the time of an earthquake <note>original: "Kshitikampana"</note>, or the time a star falls from the sky <note>original: "Tarapata," referring to meteors</note>, or during the eclipses of the Sun and Moon, the vow should not be undertaken.

> When Venus and the Moon are in their states of infancy or old age, the wise say that the 
> ritual procedure for the sacred thread initiation of a boy should not occur. 8 
> From the time of an earthquake, or the falling of a star from the heavens, or 
> during an eclipse of the Sun or Moon, the learned do not perform the vow. 4 
> If a comet <note>original: "Ketu"</note> appears in the first month, it causes the 
> failure of the ritual's success...

Regarding the appearance of a comet <term>Ketu: a comet or an astronomical tail, often viewed as a malefic omen in ancient astrology</term>, the prohibition of the vow lasts for an entire year. If a comet reaches its rising point during the first month, it is like a thorn or a disturbance created by the Titans. It is said that such a sighting destroys the auspiciousness of the rite.

One should perform the **vow** for the duration of a full year; if it is not carried out correctly, the fruit of the labor will be as fleeting as a **loosened knot** <note>original: "shithilavat," referring to something slack or unstable</note>. 1

### Prohibitions Regarding the Expunged and Intercalary Months

Now, the text prohibits the performance of vows during the "expunged month" and similar times. The wise state that any major vow performed during these periods results in the practitioner being declared a **breaker of vows** <term>Avakirni: a person who has failed to maintain the purity or discipline of their religious initiation</term>. It is said that at such a time, the spiritual merit of the land **sinks into a dark abyss**.

In the **expunged month** <term>Kshaya-masa: a rare lunar month that is "dropped" from the calendar when two solar transitions occur within one lunar month</term> or the **intercalary month** <term>Adhika-masa: an extra "leap" month added to the lunar calendar to keep it aligned with the seasons</term>, one should recognize that the "good time" is obstructed, much like the heavy rains of the monsoon hinder travel. Because of the nature of these times—the "expunged" and "extra" months—any vow undertaken is considered "swallowed" or lost. In the land of **Bharat** <note>India</note>, a vow performed now is called "interrupted," and the merit is said to be destroyed.

### On the Transits of Jupiter and Venus

A year that is **devoid of the auspicious influence of Jupiter and Venus** <note>original: "Guru-Shukra-mukta-samvatsara"</note> is declared by the learned to be harmful for the commencement of rituals. 12

In whatever **year** the **retrograde transit** <term>Vakra-sankramana: the apparent backward motion of a planet through a zodiac sign</term> of Jupiter is observed, that entire year is affected by that movement.

Now, the characteristics of the "short" and "extra" years are explained. If a year is identified by the wise as being **"freed from Jupiter’s transit"** <note>original: "Guru-sankramana-mukta"</note>, it means the planet Jupiter does not move into a new zodiac sign during that entire lunar year. Such a year, as well as a year lacking the transit of the planet Venus, is considered unfavorable for the performance of sacred rites. 13

**Now he speaks of the purification of planetary transits for the investiture of the sacred thread** <term>Vratabandha: the ritual of binding the 'vow' or the sacred thread ceremony (Upanayana)</term>. The purification for the initiation ceremony does not come from the transit alone <term>Gochara: the current movement or transit of planets through the zodiac</term>. Rather, one must observe the purification through the strength of Jupiter <term>Brihaspati: the planet Jupiter, essential for determining auspicious times for education and rituals</term>. This superior purification is to be looked for on both sides of the transit. In the month of **Chaitra** <note>March–April</note>, when the **Sun** <note>original: "surye"</note> is in **Aries** <note>original: "mitre" or "mesha"</note>, purification occurs. > Purification is not seen by the transit alone; a higher purification must be observed through the celestial strength [of Jupiter]. During the rite in the month of Chaitra, when the Sun is in the three houses... **18** This should not be done when **Venus** <term>Shukra: the planet Venus</term> is in an inauspicious state or setting, according to the teachings of the teacher Parashara. The bond of initiation should not be made when the Sun is in the month of **Pausha** <note>December–January</note> or in the sign of **Capricorn** <note>original: "mriga," literally the deer, referring to Makara/Capricorn</note>. **19**

The ancient sages who understand these mysteries have spoken regarding the bond of the ceremony. Some say that even if the Sun is in **Pisces** <note>original: "meene"</note>, it can be purifying. Furthermore, in the month of **Phalguna** <note>February–March</note> or the month of **Pausha**, if the Sun is in the sign of **Gemini** <term>Mithuna: the zodiac sign of the twins</term> or in **Capricorn** <note>original: "mriga-stha" or "makara-stha"</note>, it is considered auspicious for the ritual. **12 18**

**Again, he speaks of the subsequent determination of timing:** When the **Sun** <note>original: "hamsa" — literally "swan," a poetic term for the Sun in astrological texts</note> is in **Aries** <note>original: "mesha-rashi"</note>, the sage **Devala** and others consider this the proper time for the commencement of the activities for the sixty-vow rite. The practitioners of silence <term>Maunin: those observing a vow of silence or ascetic yogis</term> and yogis performed these rites then. In which season? When the Sun has definitely entered the sign of Aries. **Vyasa** and other knowers of the inner law speak of the excellence of this timing. Is it not so? Or rather, it is when the month of **Vaishakha** <note>April–May</note> is reached. **10** He then describes the fruit of the binding of the vow according to traditional conduct: regarding the vow, even in the lower...

<margin>Main text 6. Righteous asceticism</margin>

When the Sun is in Aries, **Devala** and others consider the commencement of the ritual activities to be fully sufficient. **Vyasa** and others who know the sacred law <term>Dharmavida: scholars or sages well-versed in the Dharma-shastras</term> speak with certainty; they say it is not to be done unless one has taken refuge in the month of **Madhava** <note>original: "Madhava-ashrite" — Madhava is another name for the lunar month of Vaishakha</note>. **1** Regarding the vow: in the month of **Tapasyu** <note>original: "tapasya" — an ancient name for the month of Phalguna (February–March)</note>, the results are varied. In the seventh portion of **Phalguna**, and in the midst of **Vaishakha**, when the Sun is obtained in the desired position, and **Venus** <note>original: "shukre"</note> is auspicious...

Because of this, if the rite is performed during the full moon in these three months, it leads to the attainment of knowledge. Furthermore, in the seventh part of Phalguna, if the rite is performed during these three months, it results in long-lasting heat or distress. Again, in the midst of **Vaishakha** and **Chaitra** <note>March–April</note>, the vow is considered most desirable for the sake of the highest goal. Furthermore, the completion [of the rite] should occur before the month of **Ashadha** <note>June–July</note>; otherwise, the vow becomes a source of distress for the cows and for **Saraswati** <note>The Goddess of speech and learning, implying that the education following the initiation will be hindered</note>. This is the meaning. For these two, there is an absence of distress [if timed correctly]. This is not the case for others. **21**

It is said that the ground should be prepared.

The **Brahmins** <term>Vipra: members of the priestly class</term>, who are like the tip of the sacrificial grass, should perform the ritual of the **Maunji** <term>the sacred girdle made of Munja grass</term> and the work of "piercing the vow" <note>addressing the overlap of ritual timings</note> in the **Spring** season <note>Vasanta</note>; this is what remains to be done.

The commentator **Hemadri** <note>a famous 13th-century scholar of Hindu law</note> says this is based on the mountain-like foundations of the texts. Likewise, for those **born from the arms** <term>Bahujāta: the Kshatriyas or warrior class</term>, the work of the girdle should be done in the summer or the **Heat** season <note>Grīṣma</note>. For the others, it should be in the month of **Vaishakha** <note>April–May</note> or during the **Rainy season** <note>Prāvṛṣa</note>, or again in the summer heat. **18**

Now, he speaks in the **Upajati** meter <note>another classical 11-syllable meter</note>:
The work of the girdle and the "piercing of the vow" for the **Brahmins** is as stated before. For the **warrior class** <note>original: "bāhujānā"</note>, it is indeed in the summer heat. For the **merchants and farmers** <term>Viśāṃ: the Vaishya class</term>, it should be during the rainy season or the summer. **15** When these timings are measured and the king follows the two paths, there is no time remaining. When the three classes are thus measured, it is prescribed. **15** Regarding the three "empty" days, he speaks of the measurement of the seventh day.

Now he shows the **Vrata-vedha** <note>vow interference</note> during the **waxing moon** <term>Śuklapakṣa: the bright fortnight</term>. In this matter, the experts say that when the vow is performed, if even **five kalas** <note>a minute unit of time, approx. 1.6 minutes</note> remain of the previous day, it is considered "interference." If only five kalas remain, the Moon becomes the "King" <note>the dominant astrological influence</note>. At that time, it is prescribed for the three classes as the vow is completed. **15**

Now he forbids the **Galagraha** <term>literally "seizing the throat": specific days when Vedic study is prohibited</term> during the "vow interference."
The **Galagraha** is always continuous. One should avoid it during the three **Rikta** <term>Empty days: the 4th, 9th, and 14th lunar days, considered inauspicious for new beginnings</term>, specifically the ninth and the fourteenth days.

# On the Planetary Lords of the Ritual

Now, salutations to the Lord of the Vedas <note>original: "Vedasvamine namah"</note>. Thus, as established by the skilled scholars <term>Panditas: learned masters of traditional Sanskrit lore</term> in the proper sequence:

The lords of the **Vedas** <note>likely referring to the planetary associations with the different Vedic branches</note> are as follows: Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> is the master, followed by Venus <note>original: "Sukra"</note>, Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note>, and Mercury <note>original: "Budha"</note>. These are also the lords of the **girdles** <term>Mekhalas: the ceremonial waist-belts made of grass or leather worn during the initiation ceremony</term>.

The practitioner who performs these rites according to the tradition is mentioned in the scriptures of each specific Vedic branch. 25.

### The Auspicious Days for the Castes

Now, he explains the specific days of the week associated with the different castes <note>original: "varnas"</note> for the ritual. It is said for the **twice-born** <term>Dvija: "twice-born," referring to the three upper castes—Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya—who undergo initiation</term>:

*   For the **Brahmins** <note>original: "Vipra"</note>, the days of Jupiter <note>original: "Harijya/Guru"</note> and the Sun <note>original: "Arka"</note> are prescribed. 
*   For the **princes** <note>original: "Rajaputras"; referring to the Kshatriyas or warrior caste</note>, the day of Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> is the primary lord in the sequence of the scriptures. 

<margin>Vasishtha 6.11 <note>Citation of the Vasishtha Samhita, an authoritative text on ritual and astrology</note></margin>

The five types of girdles and the conduct of the practitioner are thus described. 25. For the twice-born, when the lords of the planets like Jupiter and the Sun are in favorable positions, the **Sacred Thread Ceremony** <term>Upavita Karma: the ritual of investing a student with the sacred thread</term> should be performed. This ensures the fulfillment of one's own religious duty <note>original: "Svadharma"</note>.

If one performs the ritual on the day associated with their own caste <note>original: "sva-varna"</note>, it grants the full merit of their religious path. For a Brahmin, the ceremony is best performed on the day of Jupiter or the Sun. If such a day is unavailable, one must make a dedicated effort to find the next most suitable alignment for the Brahmin castes, for without the proper planetary strength, the vow may lack its full spiritual power. 30.

### The Rituals of the Atharvaveda

Now follows the section on the **Atharvaveda** <note>The fourth Veda, traditionally associated with both everyday domestic rituals and powerful transformative spells</note>. Regarding this, the text mentions "Vala" and the others in a group of six constellations for those who follow the Atharvaveda traditions. At the conclusion of the Atharvaveda study, it is asked: by what means and by whom is it told? The term **Vala-nihanta** <note>original: "Vala-nihan," meaning 'The Slayer of Vala'</note> refers to the god **Indra** <note>The King of the Gods and wielder of the thunderbolt</note>, who is the one who struck down the demon Vala.

As stated in the **Abhidhanachintamani** <term>Abhidhanachintamani: a famous 12th-century synonym lexicon or dictionary composed by the scholar Hemachandra</term>, the term refers to Indra who strikes with his thunderbolt. Whether in the context of ritual battle or the mastery of the senses, Indra is the one who overcomes the power of Vala. The constellations mentioned are: **Shravana** <note>The star of "Hearing" or "The Ear," associated with the transmission of sacred knowledge</note>; the star of the lineage of **Kashyapa** and **Aditi** which is **Punarvasu** <note>The "Return of the Light" constellation; Aditi is the mother of the gods</note>; the star of the blowing wind, **Anila**, which is **Svati** <note>Presided over by Vayu, the god of wind</note>; the star of **Mitra**, which is **Anuradha** <note>Mitra is the deity of friendship and oaths</note>; and the star of **Savitr** or the Sun, which is **Hasta** <note>The "Hand" constellation, symbolizing skill and craftsmanship</note>.

The slayer of Vala <gloss>Indra</gloss>, the son of Kashyapa, the Wind, Mitra, and Savitr—these are the powerful lords of the assembly. With these six constellations, including the Seven Sages <note>The Big Dipper or Ursa Major</note>, the cycle of thirty-five ritual elements is completed. Starting from the planet **Venus** <note>original: "Shukra"</note> and the other heavenly bodies, the mind is settled through these practices. He who carries the sacred vessel across the ocean of life finds that even the gods grant their presence here. In the pairing of these stars, what is their nature? They are like the breath of the world, flowing through the sacred rites. 35. Here, in the *Tilaka* <note>A commentary or "mark" of explanation</note>, it is said that one should not be deluded; once the ritual is released and the mind is purified, it is established. What does it say then? It speaks of the path of the Vedas and the various ways the stars like **Anuradha** and the others, starting from Venus, proceed in their course.

# The Hymn of the Golden Burden
<note>original: "Hemabhārṇistavaḥ." This title likely refers to a specific hymn dedicated to a solar deity or a ritual involving gold, often associated with the preservation of sacred energy.</note>

<margin>This is divine speech, which accords with the speech of humans. The Golden Source consists of thirty-two measures <note>original: "masī," likely referring to a specific unit of poetic or temporal measurement used in this tradition</note>.</margin>

The directions given in the spoken text are certainly to be heard and followed in practice, as established by the Vedas. This encompasses the various divisions of the gods, starting with the **Thirty-Three** <term>Tridaśādo: a collective term for the principal Vedic pantheon, literally meaning the 'Thirty' (rounded from thirty-three)</term>. 

Regarding the constellation **Ashvini** <note>The first lunar mansion, symbolized by horsemen and representing new beginnings and healing</note>, it is through this that one attains wealth and the fulfillment of the rituals. In the context of the ritual application, it is also stated that the hearing of the sacred word must be carried out correctly. This involves the principle of phonetic attraction, where the sounds are brought together because they rely on a shared foundation. 

In the forest-dwelling traditions, one must avoid certain phonetic prohibitions, such as those seen in the phrase "the tawny deer" <note>original: "kapilā eṇī"</note>. These rules prevent the corruption of the sacred sound. In this context, the comparison is made to "two jewels" <term>maṇī ive: a famous technical example in Sanskrit grammar where two vowels remain distinct and do not merge into a single sound (Sandhi)</term>. Because these sounds are distinct—like two deities—they do not merge, preserving their individual power. This is seen when observing the phonetic union in the vision of the sacred texts.

The **Triṣṭubh** meter <note>A Vedic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</note> is employed for the ten directions and the thirty gods. This is used whenever the form of the ritual is established according to the sequence. 

Regarding the constellation of **Pushan** <term>Pauṣne: another name for the Nakshatra Revatī, presided over by the deity Pushan, the nourisher and protector of travelers</term>, some scholars say that it contains the essence of the wind's fragrance. This constellation resides in the realm of the Earth. 

The **Hymn of the Golden Burden** should be recited with the beautiful and well-measured verses of the **Triṣṭubh** meter. This involves the contraction of sounds based on the proximity of the deities. For the wise who understand all the divisions of the Vedas, there is no difference in the ultimate goal of these sounds. For the **Brahmins** <note>The priestly class responsible for the preservation of the Vedas</note>, the distinction of the constellations like **Revati** is explained through their presiding deities. Some experts describe this as the movement of the **Gandharvas** <note>Celestial musicians and guardians of the sacred Soma</note> through the air. The constellations mentioned—**Svati**, the stars of the **Vasus** <note>A group of eight elemental deities</note>, and others—are the ones through which the wealth of the sacrifice is distributed.

<summary>This page discusses the technical phonetic and metrical requirements for reciting the Hymn of the Golden Burden, emphasizing the use of the Triṣṭubh meter and the auspicious influence of constellations like Ashvini and Revati.</summary>

# Now he describes the results of the planetary influences and the aspect of Jupiter within the ritual vow

As for the lineage of the one who bears the staff <note>original: "daṇḍrivatī-kula"</note>, the power of their influence becomes like the sun. Whether it be the gods, the ancestors, or those whom the demons cannot overcome—when Venus <note>original: "Shukre"</note> or Jupiter <note>original: "Gurau"</note> is in the position of the celestial priest <term>Purodhas: The family priest or spiritual advisor; in astrology, this refers to the guiding influence of the benevolent planets</term>, or when the Lord of the Twice-born <note>original: "dvija-vibhu," referring to Jupiter</note> is present, the results are twofold. Such a person is blessed with children and is recognized as a leader. When the three-fold path is reached and the influence of malefic planets <note>original: "pāpa"</note> is subdued, the vow is successful. [41]

Now, regarding the two poets <note>original: "kāvya-haye," likely referring to the artistic or prophetic nature of Venus and Jupiter</note>: when the first priest of the gods, Jupiter, or the Lord of the Twice-born is in an auspicious division <note>original: "maṇḍala"</note>, the family lineage is preserved. When this occurs, the message of the beloved is reached. [42]

He describes the arrival of prosperity <note>original: "lakṣmīm āha"</note> through the position of the Moon. If the Moon is situated in a quadrant <term>Kendra-gata: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart, which represent the "pillars" of a person's life</term>, and is associated with the planets of the vow, the individual becomes a consumer of wealth and a protector of the people. [44]

He explains further: In this world, if the Moon is in an angle, even a woman or a Shudra <note>meaning those outside the traditional priestly or warrior castes in this historical context</note> will receive favorable results. If it is in a strong "Thorn" house <term>Kaṇṭaka: A synonym for Kendra, meaning an angular house that provides a sharp, defining structure to the life</term>, specifically the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th, one becomes a servant of the king <note>original: "nṛ-jīvī sevaka"</note> by the king's favor. Furthermore, if Venus is in such a "Thorn" house, one becomes a worker of deeds <term>Karma-kāraka: One who performs work or fulfills their destiny through action</term>. Again, if the Lord of the Earth <note>referring to a planetary ruler</note> is in an angle, the results are beneficial for all classes. Finally, if Jupiter, acting as the celestial priest, is in an angular house, one becomes an enjoyer of vast wealth and resources <note>original: "bhūri-gaṇārtha-bhuk"</note> and a possessor of great fame and riches. [45]

Regarding what was not spoken or followed in the tradition <note>original: "na gadito nagatika..." interpreted as a deviation from standard practice</note>, how can the initiation ritual <term>Upanayana</term> <note>the "sacred thread" ceremony marking the start of a student's Vedic education</note> be desired or performed during a three-day period? > Someone said: At the conclusion of the day, when the cows are released, and the three-day ritual is performed, it is called the initiation ritual. In this procedure, when the impurities are removed [42], the root of the people's time is established. At the time of the ritual for the twice-born, because of the power of the time, the binding of the ritual is regulated by
> -> one's own action [4]. <-

The heat remains until the end, and the path is illuminated [45]. When the gathering of light fades, everything is seen according to the time of the ritual. This is for the certainty of the people's knowledge. In the time of the world, when each ritual reaches its own proper time, the regulation is preserved. Why? Because the time of the world is like the protector of the ages. Thus, in the absence of the proper time for all rituals, the regulation of the protection of the ritual is indeed achieved through one's own action <term>Karma</term>.

# Commentary on the Delight of Astrology

### On the Sacred Thread and the Return of the Student

If the time for the sacred thread ceremony occurs during an improper season <note>original: "akalavrita," referring to a ritual performed outside the astrologically sanctioned window</note>, one should check if there is prosperity, joy, or a favorable planetary position. Even if the timing is mixed, if favorable planets are present, the initiation should be written down. Regarding the <term>Upavita</term> <note>the sacred thread worn by the "twice-born" classes</note>, the master of the household proceeds with the ritual. Again, there are fifty-three ways the root of this ritual is applied. [53]

Now, regarding the young student <note>original: "vato," a lad or celibate student</note> who has gone to the teacher's house: after the observation of the gift of cows performed by the maternal uncle <note>original: "matula-krita-go-vara-darshana"; the maternal uncle traditionally plays a major role in the student's life</note>, and having attained knowledge, the young student’s return to his own home occurs. For what reason? It is performed for the sake of the family lineage. The student returns after being purified by the sacred knowledge, much like a warrior is refined by his weapon. What is the nature of this return? It is like the moon emerging from behind a cloud, gaining beauty and radiance. What else characterizes this return?

-> When the time has arrived, just as previously stated, the student returns on a fruitful day. <-
-> Accompanied by the sounds of the kinsmen, the maternal uncle brings the young student home. <-

"Accompanied by the sounds of the kinsmen's forest" is indicated by the use of the third grammatical case to show accompaniment. This refers to the sounds of kettledrums and other instruments played by the gathered relatives as the maternal uncle calls the student and settles him back into the home. [54]

Now, for the sake of general understanding, all the <term>Samskaras</term> <note>the life-cycle sacraments that purify and sanctify an individual at different stages of life</note> are written here:
1. **Conception** <note>original: "Garbhadhana," the ritual to ensure a healthy conception</note>
2. **Ensuring a male child** <note>original: "Pumsavana," performed during pregnancy</note>
3. **Parting the hair** <note>original: "Simantonnayana," a prenatal ritual for the mother's well-being</note>
4. **Birth-ritual** <note>original: "Jatakarma," performed immediately after birth</note>
5. **Naming** <note>original: "Namakarana"</note>
6. **First solid food** <note>original: "Annaprashana"</note>
7. **First haircut** <note>original: "Chudakarana," often referred to as the tonsure</note>
8. **Initiation** <note>original: "Upavitake" or Upanayana, the sacred thread ceremony</note>
9. **Gift of cows** <note>original: "Godana," marking the first shaving of the beard</note>
10. **Sun-vow** <note>original: "Adityavrata," a specific student vow</note>

# The Enumeration of Sacrifices and Sacraments

First is the offering to all beings <note>original: "Bhuta-yajna"</note>, followed by the offering to the ancestors, the offering to the Creator <note>original: "Brahma-yajna"</note>, the offering to humanity <note>hospitality to guests</note>, and the daily fire offerings. These five constitute the first group of seven—the "cooked" ritual establishments <note>original: "Paka-samstha," referring to simpler domestic sacrifices</note>. Included in the traditional works of ritual law are the various seasonal rites such as the Spring sacrifice.

The second group includes the establishment of the sacred fires, the daily fire-oblation <note>original: "Agnihotra"</note>, the new moon and full moon sacrifices, and the four-month seasonal sacrifices <note>original: "Chaturmasya"</note>, which total five. Additionally, there are the offerings of the first fruits and the Sautramani sacrifice <note>a rite involving the healing of the senses</note>. These are known as the "Foremost among Offerings." [6]

The third group consists of the Seven Soma Sacrifices <note>complex Vedic rituals involving the pressing of the Soma plant</note>: the <term>Agnishtoma</term>, <term>Atyagnishtoma</term>, <term>Ukthya</term>, <term>Shodashin</term>, <term>Atiratra</term>, <term>Vajapeya</term>, and the <term>Aptoryama</term>. These seven are known throughout all the sacred scriptures as the establishments of Soma.

Following these rituals are the virtues: tranquility, self-control, and patience, which are spoken of as the power of the soul.

The limbs of Yoga are also to be known:
1. Restraint <note>original: "Yama"</note>
2. Purity <note>original: "Shaucha"</note>
3. Observance <note>original: "Niyama"</note>
4. Breath control <note>original: "Pranayama"</note>
5. Withdrawal of the senses <note>original: "Pratyahara"</note>
6. Meditation <note>original: "Dhyana"</note>
7. Concentration <note>original: "Dharana"</note>

These are the limbs of Yoga, along with the eight qualities of the soul. In total, the forty-eight sacraments were explained by the sage Gautama. A man who is consecrated by these forty-eight rites is truly a "Supreme Person" <note>original: "Purushottama," an idealized or perfected human being</note>. [10]

Now, these are named in order:
1. <term>Pumsavana</term> <note>the rite to ensure a male child</note>
2. <term>Simanta</term> <note>parting the hair of the pregnant mother</note>
3. <term>Jatakarma</term> <note>birth rites</note>
4. <term>Namakarana</term> <note>naming ceremony</note>
5. <term>Annaprashana</term> <note>the first feeding of solid food</note>
6. <term>Chaula</term> <note>the first tonsure or haircut</note>
7. <term>Upanayana</term> <note>initiation and investiture of the sacred thread</note>

Following these are the five vows of Vedic study and the four stages of life, concluding with the ritual of <term>Vivaha</term> <note>marriage</note>.

# The Forty Sacraments and the Virtues of the Soul

The traditional Shrauta <note>rituals based on high Vedic revelation</note> actions are fourfold: the **Shukriyam** [1], the **Shakkaram** [2], the **Vratika** [3], and the **Upanishad** [4]. To these are added the **Five Great Sacrifices** [5], the **Seven Cooked Sacrifice Establishments** [7], the **Seven Oblation Sacrifice Establishments** [7], and the **Seven Soma Establishments** [7]. When all these are combined, they total twenty-four rituals. In poetic and legal treatises, it is said there are **Forty Sacraments** <note>original: "Chatvarimshat-samskara"</note>.

Furthermore, there are the Eight Virtues of the Soul <note>original: "Atmaguna"</note>:
1. **Self-control** <note>Danti</note>
2. **Forbearance** <note>Atrastya; likely referring to Kshanti or patience</note>
3. **Purity** <note>Shaucham</note>
4. **Ease** <note>Anayasa; freedom from over-exertion</note>
5. **Auspiciousness** <note>Mangala</note>
6. **Generosity** <note>Akarpanya; freedom from misery or stinginess</note>
7. **Detachment** <note>Aspriha; freedom from worldly desire</note>
<note>The text lists these as the qualities that make a person truly "sacramental" beyond mere ritual performance.</note>

Thus, in the final portion of the legal treatises, the forty sacraments are described. Some people in this world, endowed with various forms of excellence, say that the sacraments are meant for those who have conquered their senses. Therefore, here we write of the nature of the sacraments for those who seek victory over the self, following the form of the sacred syllable **Om**.

-> Twelve are the paths of the sun; I offer the oblation to the one who is praised as the lord of cows, Svaha! [54] <-

In this world, certain masters—deluded by their own visions or perhaps establishing their own authority—namely the **Jains** <note>Arhat</note> [1], the **Buddhists** <note>Saugata</note> [2], the **Vaisheshikas** [3], the **Logicians** [4], the **Samkhyas** [5], and the **Materialists** <note>Charvaka</note> [6], follow the "Light of Reality" <note>Tattvaloka</note> to define the nature of the Self. They discuss the relationship between the cognizer <term>Pramata</term>, the object of knowledge <term>Prameya</term>, and the means of knowledge <term>Pramana</term>. 

Even the Jains, who understand the assembly of all living beings, accept the necessity of sacraments beginning from the union of life-elements <note>conception</note> up to the "Coronation of the Great King" <note>Maharajyabhisheka; likely referring to the final spiritual attainment</note>. Even though their views differ, they are not entirely disconnected. As it is stated in their scriptures: all the gods, demons, and lords of men perform these rites. On those days, even they follow the path of the Vedas and the sacraments. Thus, the beginning of the ritual process is described here.

### The Rite of Initiation
Regarding the **Procedure for Initiation** <note>Upanayana; the sacred thread ceremony</note> in this tradition: it is for the **Jaina Brahmins** <note>A specific priestly class within the Jaina social structure, distinct from the Hindu Brahmin caste</note> and generally for the **Vaishyas** <note>The merchant and agricultural class</note>.

Because it is possible, the rule for wearing the **Conquered Sacred Thread** <note>original: Jitopavita; in Jaina tradition, this symbolizes victory over the senses and worldly passions</note> is described. Here, they do not carry the three-fold Vedic fire. For the householder, the wife performs the ritual with the water vessel from her own hand. The vow of the sage is the cause of all causes, an inner realization granted by the divine. It is not merely the sprinkling of water or the outward ritual. Thus, the Brahmin is one who is refined by these sacraments. For this reason, the method of the day's purification is described, following the process of the sacraments...

By that prescribed rule, one should proceed with the breath of life. Regarding the <unclear>Asmapitro</unclear> <note>possibly a corrupted reference to parental rites</note>, it is mentioned in the "five occasions" that relate to specific queries. These include the twelfth-day rites, the keeping of vigils, the **Naming Ceremony** <note>original: Namakarana</note>, the first entry into a great house, the ceremonial feasts, the rites for prosperity and growth, the "time-speech" rites <note>original: Kalavada; likely a regional term for specific auspicious announcements</note>, and various local customs such as the "binding" and "smearing" rituals.

Whether it concerns the removal of obstacles or the taking up of new protections, even the king’s mind is occupied by these various festivities. Regarding this, the text of the **Traditional Law** <note>original: Smriti</note> says: "Supreme desire is achieved on earth, and the desire for entering a home is made fruitful."

Through these two methods, there is a movement toward the reason for the feast; when the food is bound into a morsel <note>original: Pindabaddha</note>, it is for the sake of the heart alone. Lighting the fire is for the sake of illumination. The "time-speech" is well-known, as are the local customs of binding and smearing. For the sake of mutual exchange, it is said that "one speaks," and for the sake of supporting growth, it is "wearing." In the acquisition of the arts and similar endeavors, even for kings and others, one performs these activities. 

From the **Conception Rite** <note>original: Garbhadana</note> onwards, one seeks these festive curiosities. Regarding these conception rites and the entry into various states, the *Scripture of Mayadeva* <note>original: Mayadeva Shastra; an architectural or ritual manual</note> and others describe these activities. It was also spoken by the **Lord Vishnu** <note>here cited as a traditional authority on social conduct</note>, following the scriptures: one should avoid the appearance of improper conduct and remain like an omniscient **Kevali** <note>a perfected, all-knowing being in Jainism</note> in the midst of worldly dealings, as the verses state.

In the world, it is even so; even if there are those who maintain their life-breaths now, one should not violate local worldly customs <note>original: Laukikachara</note> even in one's mind. This is in accordance with the **Jain Doctrine**.

Now, concerning the rituals for the young student, if he does not perform them, then the connection to the discourse of the assembly is stated here: **"When it is performed..."** After the naming ceremony, the very speech of those reciting the Vedas <note>original: Vedapathatam</note> is heard. When this is known and performed, the inquiry is explained through the "Manakali" dance <note>possibly a reference to a rhythmic or celebratory recitation</note>. For what purpose is the **Sacred Tradition** <note>original: Agama; refers to established scriptural authority</note> invoked? Tradition encompasses the six lineages. By relying on this tradition, these **Sciences** <note>original: Vidya</note> proceed for the sake of protecting the moment and for the accomplishment of spiritual power. "For accomplishment" means for the sake of attainment. 

Now, the text describes the general inquiry using the **Upachitra** meter <note>a Sanskrit poetic meter consisting of eleven syllables</note> and the **Padakulaka** meter: **"Known..."**

<margin>This relates to the language of speech; so says Hemachandra: 1.</margin>

When the **Commencement of Tradition** <note>original: Agamarambha</note> is performed, it is said to be the beginning of the inquiry. This is for the sake of perfecting the sciences of the scriptures through the various branches of tradition. For one whose speech is purified, the dawn of knowledge occurs in a non-dual form. **"The Sage of Speech"** <note>original: Vagarshi</note>—

->The beginning of the inquiry into that language occurs on an excellent and auspicious day. 1.<-

<gloss>Known: continuous or eternal</gloss>
O Sage of Speech, the seekers of knowledge—the students—behold the **Beginning of Study** <note>original: Vidyarambha</note> in this world. They do so to obtain the qualities of eloquence and poetic skill, which are as refreshing as a bath in the essence of language. On which excellent day should this occur? Among the gods, the "excellent" day is the Day of the Lord, which refers to the **Northern Solstice** <note>original: Uttarayana; the six-month period when the sun travels north, considered spiritually auspicious</note>. Furthermore, in what state should one be? It should occur when speech is purified, when the Vedic scriptures are mastered, when there is faith in the Teacher (Guru), and when good deeds are on the rise.

### The Constellations for the General Commencement of Study

Now, he describes the **Constellations** <note>term: Nakshatra; the 27 divisions of the sky through which the moon passes</note> for the general commencement of education. He says "by night," referring to the "Night-stalkers" <note>original: Naktamchara; a reference to Rahu, the shadow planet believed to cause obstacles or eclipses</note>. It is declared by scholars that the beginning of study is auspicious when these specific influences are accounted for. The "Night-stalker" Rahu can cause impurities; however, just as water-lily leaves remain untouched by water, these instructions help one overcome all obstacles. When study is seized by an obstacle, it is not auspicious. Which constellations are meant? Those like **Purva Bhadrapada** <note>A constellation often associated with fire or transformation</note>. In the sky, the wisdom of the constellations belonging to the gods is used to invoke success. Furthermore, these are characterized by the "trembling of limbs" <note>original: lola-lalahanga; likely a poetic description of planetary motion or the energetic state of the student</note> and the presence of youthful energy. 54.

The commencement of study is declared by the wise when it is free from the diseases and obstacles of the "Night-stalkers," and coincides with the constellations of **Phalguni** <note>The "reddish" stars, often associated with prosperity and marriage</note> and others. When the constellations associated with **Parjanya** <note>The Vedic deity of rain and thunder</note> are honored by scholars, and the Great Ones have directly witnessed the cessation of hindrances, then study may begin. Even if there are obstacles to education on certain days, writing down "gentle results" <note>original: saumya-phala; refers to the positive influence of Mercury or generally auspicious outcomes</note> may sometimes mitigate them. 6.

Now, in the *Bhujangaprayata* meter <note>term: Bhujangaprayata; a rhythmic poetic structure consisting of four segments of twelve syllables each, literally meaning "the gliding of a serpent"</note>, the calculation for the beginning of education is described by the wise and ever-awakened scholars. # The Commencement of the Treatise on Grammar

A skillful scholar <term>Kriti-pandit; a learned person who is also adept in ritual practice</term> should begin the study of the scriptures at the proper time. Specifically, this refers to the commencement of the **Agamas** <note>original: Agamas; here referring to the traditional Vedic scriptures</note> and **Grammar** <term>Vyakarana; the science of linguistic analysis, considered the "mouth" of the Vedas</term>. Alternatively, "Agama" may refer directly to the **Veda**.

On the days of the wise ones—namely **Mercury** <note>original: Budha</note>, the peaceful **Saturn** <note>original: Shanto</note>, **Venus** <note>original: Shukra</note>, and again **Mercury**—when these days are present, one should begin. ## The Commencement of Sankhya and Other Philosophies

3. **Vishakha**

## Now, the Timing for Studying the Sciences of Trade and Victory is Told

For the study of the **Science of Victory** <term>Jaitra-vidya; specialized knowledge used to ensure success in conquest, debate, or competition</term> and the **Science of Trade** <note>original: "Vipana-shastra"; commerce or marketplace dynamics</note>, one should remain within the specific **Astrological Hour** <term>Hora; a division of time roughly equal to one hour, ruled by a specific planet</term>.

The beginning of such studies should always take place during the day for the **Science of Drama and Music**. 

Those who possess the power of disciplined practice <note>original: "Yogavadbhir"</note> should observe the specific portions of the day. If the application of this knowledge is performed during the correct planetary hours, it becomes resonant and successful.

<margin>
Here follows the rule for **Mondays** regarding the results of disciplined practice.
</margin>

The **Science of Victory** brings intelligence and success when it is "awakened" at the proper time. What is this state? It is when the **Sun** is in a specific position. Regarding the directions, one should look to the West, which is the direction of the **Lord of the Waters** <term>Varuna; the Vedic deity of the celestial ocean and the guardian of the western quarter</term>. After bathing and cleansing oneself at night, one should proceed. Under the influence of the stars **Shravana** and **Revati**, and considering the influence of **Venus** <note>original: "Shukra"</note>, the student gains the power to overcome obstacles.

# On the Science of the Foreigners (Yavana-vidya)

Regarding the **Science of the Foreigners** <term>Yavana-vidya; historically refers to Greek astrology and mathematical sciences integrated into Indian tradition</term>, the text explains its commencement. This includes the study of languages <note>original: "bhasha"</note>, fierce dialects, and the rhythmic patterns of foreign speech. When beginning this study, one must observe when the **Sharp Planets** <term>Teevra; typically referring to the influence of Mars or Saturn</term> are in favorable alignment.

If the start occurs on a day ruled by **Jupiter** <term>Guru; the planet of wisdom and expansion</term>, it is considered highly auspicious for attaining wealth through this knowledge. The radiance of this science is said to shine brightly when the student engages with the speech of the "fierce" or "harsh" lineages. Such an endeavor is governed by **Varuna** <note>original: "Varuna-kala"; the deity of the waters and the cosmic order</note>, who acts as the lord of these specific durations of time.

### Now, he prohibits the worship of mantras and related rituals [during certain times].

The scholars and learned pundits <note>original: "surayah panditah"</note> declare that for the service and worship of **mantras** and **yantras** <term>Yantra; a mystical geometric diagram used in meditation and ritual</term>, as well as for initiation <note>original: "upayanay"; the thread ceremony or start of studies</note>, taking vows of renunciation, and for the sake of a son, these two actions [service and worship] do not grant the desired position or goal. This applies when the Sun is in the house of **Aquarius** <note>original: "Kumbha"</note> or at home. If the Sun is in the sign of **Pisces** <note>original: "Meena"</note>, or even if it returns to **Aries** <note>original: "Arka" / "Meenake"</note>, one should not perform these rituals. Furthermore, one should not begin when the planet **Venus** <note>original: "Shukra"</note> is setting <note>original: "astagate"; a state called 'combustion' where a planet is too close to the sun to be visible and is considered weakened</note>, as the purpose will be destroyed.

#### Regarding the Sun’s entry into Virgo

-><-

In the various types of worship and residence, in the movement of the sun into **Virgo** <note>original: "Kanya Sankranti"</note>, and for the practice of mantras and yantras, one should not be occupied with these if the sun is in an unfavorable position for the desired result. 3. Regarding the rituals of women: when the Sun is in the sign of **Leo** <note>original: "Hari"</note>, or during the time of the **deities' sleep**, or in an intercalary month, one should not begin. 32.

-><-

He now prohibits the specific vows <term>Vrata; a religious vow or ritual observance</term> of women. Regarding the worship and rituals of women <note>original: "varninina"; likely referring to those following a specific spiritual path or class</note>, it is not beneficial during the rising of the "Pot-Pilgrimage" <note>original: "Kumbha-tirtha"; a specific astrological or seasonal timing related to the sign of Aquarius</note>. As stated by the venerable **Hemachandra** <note>the famous 12th-century scholar and polymath</note>: when one's own foot is not firm, or when the Sun is in certain positions, the vow should not be undertaken. Furthermore, when the deities are in their period of sleep <note>original: "Devata-supti-kala"; the four-month period of Chaturmasya when Lord Vishnu is said to sleep</note>, or in an intercalary month <term>Adhika Maasa; an extra month added to the lunar calendar to keep it in sync with the solar year, generally considered inauspicious for new beginnings</term>, or when **Venus** <note>original: "Vainya"</note> or **Jupiter** <note>original: "Guru"</note> have set [are combust], the ritual is considered fruitless. 32.

Three is represented by **Agni** <note>original: "Agni"; the fire god, traditionally associated with the number 3 due to the three ritual fires</note>; three is represented by **Rama** <note>original: "Rama"; often used for the number 3 representing the three historical Ramas</note>; four is represented by the **Ashvins** <note>original: "Ashvi"; though usually 2, here grouped with 4 or referring to a specific quadrant</note>; four is represented by the **Vedas** <note>the four primary Hindu scriptures</note>; three is represented by Agni; four is represented by the **Agamas** <note>sacred tradition/scriptures</note>. These numbers define the grid. By these six compartments, the "Falcon's Net" <note>original: "syenatajjalam"</note> is formed. One should not perform the mantra without this system. The position of the head of the Mantra Deva is established; then, through three **Nakshatras** <term>Nakshatras; the 27 lunar mansions or constellations of the zodiac</term>, the mouth is formed; then, through three more Nakshatras, the throat. The six limbs and body parts are thus established. Oh! The eternal unity of the three! Here, plurality is established because of their eternal nature. As it says in the **Abhidhanachintamani** <note>a famous 12th-century Sanskrit lexicon by the scholar Hemachandra</note>: "The kings... the water... the deep red... the white." 36. This applies everywhere. 37.

Regarding the waist and the hips: these are the domains of the "sinful signs" <note>inauspicious zodiac signs</note>. For the Mantra Deva who is dancing, the two feet are placed thus. In the head, the values of **Rama** (3), the **Ashvins** (2), the **Vedas** (4), **Agni** (3), the **Ramas** (3), and the **Agamas** (4) are measured in order by the Moon <note>original: "oshadhisha"; literally "lord of the herbs," an epithet for the Moon</note>. 35. Success <note>original: "siddhi"</note> in the mantra is achieved if it is in the head; in the mouth, it grants attainment. In the throat, it brings about **Time** <note>original: "Kalakrit"; a euphemism for death or the end of a period</note> and faults. In the chest, even if there is a beginning, there is a loss of wealth and laughter.

->Regarding the grid of the three. 35.<-

The throat is formed by three Nakshatras; the hands by another three; the heart by another three. Six are here. With the **Agni** (3) in the chest... the "sinful signs" are established in the plural. The waist is formed by three more Nakshatras. The two feet are placed in the two compartments of the remaining Nakshatras. 35. Now, the results for the limbs of the Mantra-body are told: if the power of the mantra resides in the head of the **Mantra Purusha** <note>the "Mantra-Man" or personified chant</note>, and if it is measured by the Nakshatras of the month of **Chaitra** <note>March-April</note>, then the practitioner <note>original: "sadhaka"</note> will attain perfection and success in the mantra. Likewise, in the mouth, it is a giver of success. However, in the throat or neck, it is a "maker of time" <note>meaning it causes death or failure</note>. Faults and enemies...

# On the Purity of Timing and the Friendship of Mantras

Now, he explains the **Maitri** <term>Maitri; literally "friendship," referring here to the astrological compatibility between a practitioner’s birth star and the mantra they intend to use</term> and the **Chapana** <note>original: "chapana"; the ritual casting or movement of the mantra</note>, as well as the **Shuddhi** <term>Shuddhi; ritual purity or the "correctness" of the astrological alignment</term> of the time. In the practice of one's own mantra, the work should be done when there is purity. Specifically, during the auspicious time of **Shravana** <note>Shravana is one of the 27 lunar mansions (nakshatras), associated with "hearing" and considered highly auspicious for receiving knowledge</note>, it becomes beneficial for the seeker.

In that context, the **Chakra** <term>Chakra; a symbolic diagram or wheel used to calculate planetary influences</term> is "nourished by the Moon" <note>original: "indu poshita"</note>. Through this, one achieves the purity of the stars. This star-purity leads to the success of the ritual. Furthermore, there is a fire offering known as the **Homa** <term>Homa; a consecrated fire ritual where offerings are made into the flames</term> designated for **Dharma** (duty), **Dhana** (wealth), and **Kalatra** (spouse).

The practitioner <note>original: "sadhaka"</note> should perform the **Japa** <term>Japa; the meditative repetition of a mantra</term> eight times during the fire offering. This is the prescribed method. All these actions—the repetition of the mantra and the fire offering—ensure the purity of the mantra's work. By performing these during the auspicious time, the stars within the "Moon-nourished Wheel" reach a state of purity. (Verse 39)

### The Wheel of Nourishment

Now, after drawing the **Anna Chakra** <term>Anna Chakra; the "Food Wheel," a diagram used to determine how a mantra "consumes" or interacts with the practitioner's energy</term>, one should follow the sequence of the "stream of stars." Just as it is ordained, one must join the planets—the Sun, the Moon’s son <note>Mercury</note>, the Moon, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus again—to the eight parts of the mantra. (Verse 38) This refers to the **Ahuti** <term>Ahuti; the act of pouring an offering into the ritual fire</term>. (Verse 39)

Now, he speaks of what is pleasing in the **Upendravajra** meter <note>a classical Sanskrit poetic rhythm</note>. The wise person writes the wheel. With what intention or "internal heat" is this done? As it is heard in the sacred texts, the wise one holds the sequence of the wheel, which encompasses all directions. 

For the purpose of the ritual bath and the union of all factors, one should employ the following planetary identities:
*   **Ravi** is the **Sun**.
*   **Jo** <note>a shortened form of Budha-ja</note> is **Mercury**.
*   **Shukra** is the **Lord** or **Sita** <note>the "White" planet, Venus</note>.
*   **Arka** or **Ara** is **Mars**.
*   **Jiva** or **Guru** is **Jupiter**.
*   **Ketu** <note>the descending lunar node</note> and <unclear>Saturn and Rahu</unclear> are these mentioned here. (18)

### The Purification of the Ascendant for the Consecration

Now, he explains the **purification of the ascendant** <term>Lagna-shuddhi; the calculation to ensure the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon is auspicious</term> for the **consecration** <term>Abhisheka</term>. According to the scriptures, the consecration of the ruler of the earth, the **King** <note>original: "Mahipati"</note>, is declared to be most excellent when performed under specific conditions.

Under which astrological signs should this occur? Even if other factors are strong, the strength of the **ascendant** <term>Lagna</term> is paramount. He lists the auspicious signs as: **Pisces** <note>original: "Nimi"</note>, **Virgo** <note>original: "Stri" or "Kanya"</note>, **Gemini** <note>original: "Jitam" or "Mithuna"</note>, and **Taurus**. For these signs, he discusses the **hour-division** <term>Hora; a division of a zodiac sign representing roughly one hour</term>, noting that the ritual should occur during the sign's own *Hora* or that of a friendly planet.

<margin>What kind of benefic planets? Those possessing auspicious aspects and wisdom. 12</margin>

The King becomes a powerful sovereign through these influences. When **benefic planets** <term>Saumya-grahas; "gentle" planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</term> are positioned in houses other than the first, twelfth, or eighth, the ruler successfully attains the **crown-consecration** <term>Patabhisheka; the specific ritual of binding the royal fillet or crown upon the brow</term>. 

When planets reside in the **houses of growth** <term>Upachaya; the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses which signify increasing power over time</term>, the King holds the **circle of his kingdom** <note>original: "Mandala"</note> as firmly as a mountain.

He specifies the houses for the planets as follows: 
- The third (3)
- The eleventh (11)
- The sixth (6)
- The tenth (10)

Now he describes the specific "fruit" or result of the consecration based on these planetary positions. By the influence of these benefics, the lord attains the great status of the crown-consecration. This is true provided the planets avoid the following "harmful" houses: the sixth (6), twelfth (12), and eighth (8) <note>original: "Ramana, Matya, Laya"; these are coded names for the 6th, 12th, and 8th houses</note>.

# Now, the Principle of the Conjunctions of Lunar Mansions and Planets is Explained

Now, the principle of the conjunctions of planets and lunar mansions <term>Nakshatrayoga; the specific alignment of planets within the 27 lunar mansions of the Indian zodiac</term> is shown. Regarding "Fortune" <note>original: "bhagyam"; likely referring to the Nakshatra Purva-Phalguni, whose presiding deity is Bhaga, the god of fortune</note>: three parts are distributed among all the Phalguni stars. Excluding the intermediate directions, when the Moon <term>Vidhu; a poetic name for the Moon</term> is present, or when a single lunar mansion is occupied, it is the star of the vow.

In the star of the Faithful <note>original: "sati"; likely referring to a specific auspicious alignment</note>, when Mars is in the "Root" star <term>Mula; the 19th lunar mansion, associated with the core or foundation</term>, and Mercury is in conjunction with the technical point <note>original: "ddu-ddu"; a technical scribal abbreviation or symbol used in astronomical tables to denote specific degrees or subdivisions</note>. Here, whatever letters are used: the union of the **Seven Sages** <term>Saptarishi; the constellation Ursa Major or the Great Bear</term> occurs in the thirteenth vowel. From this, "Hearing" <term>Shravana; the 22nd lunar mansion, associated with listening and oral tradition</term> is born. 

Again, it is well known that the Moon's bondage occurs in the star "Later Blessed Feet" <term>Uttarabhadrapada; the 26th lunar mansion</term>. Furthermore, when the technical symbol <gloss>ddu</gloss> is at the forefront of the "Cutters" <term>Krttika; the Pleiades, the 3rd lunar mansion</term>, it is followed by the Sun <term>Arka; the Sun</term>. What is the meaning? The Sun is positioned there. 

In the star of the Noble One <note>original: "aryabhe"; referring to the Nakshatra Uttara-Phalguni</note>, there is a portion of the Infinite One <note>original: "saruna"; likely referring to Varuna or a solar deity</note>. Fortune is the ornament of the division. Knowing the fortune in the Moon, in the place of the "Root" <term>Mula</term> on earth, then this is the "Bull" <term>Vrsha; the zodiac sign Taurus</term>. The conjunction of the Sun and stars is **18**. 

Regarding the **Consecration** <term>Abhisheka; the ritual bath and crowning of a king</term>, when it occurs under such a star conjunction, he shines as a "Great Forest King" <note>original: "mahavanyarat"; likely an epithet for a Universal Monarch who rules even the wild lands</note>. He becomes the possessor of many rice-halls, peaceful and wise. This is the method for the one who has been ritually bathed **19**.

In this way, for the one who is nourished **1**, having considered the path of the "Twins" <term>Ashvini; the 1st lunar mansion</term> and the "Restrainer" <term>Yama; the deity of the Bharani star</term>, the Sun's light descends. The Sun brings peace and is a friend. When the Sun is in conjunction with the technical symbol, it is for the sake of the gods. This jewel of a king is **33**. 

Furthermore, how does "Fortune" and the other planets appear? When Saturn is in a lunar mansion and there is a star conjunction, it is **18**. Here, the influence of Saturn and the Sun is of many types **42**. When seated on the throne, the star conjunctions are as follows: if the conjunction occurs in the "Twins" <term>Ashvini</term> while the fire ritual is being performed, and the stars are auspicious, the King who is consecrated becomes a **Great Charioteer** <term>Maharatha; a warrior capable of fighting ten thousand others simultaneously</term>. What kind of ruler? A King of Kings, the lord of many halls and fortified enclosures.

# On the Assembly Hall

Now [the author] speaks of the presiding deity of the assembly hall, beginning with the word **"virtuous"** <note>original: "sati"</note>. Regarding the assembly hall <term>Sabha; a royal court or assembly hall where the king conducts business</term>, he [the king] should arrange it in the following way. He asks: what is the nature of this hall? It is excellent and proper. Furthermore, what is its nature? It is filled with valiant heroes, soldiers, and ministers. It is also filled with the splendor of ceremonial fly-whisks <term>Chamara; whisks made of yak-tail hair used as a symbol of royalty</term> and with Brahmin scholars <term>Vipra; a member of the priestly class</term> who have studied the sacred scriptures <note>original: "Agama"; traditional Vedic or post-Vedic instructional texts</note> from all sides. 

Furthermore, what is its nature? It is worthy of the king's majesty <term>Nrpa-gaurava; the dignity and weight of office appropriate for a ruler</term>. Furthermore, what is its nature? It has the shape of a bow <note>original: "chapakrti"; an arched or semi-circular architectural design</note>. Furthermore, what is its nature? The interior where the king’s throne is placed is not excessively high. Having reached such a residence, one should perform the duties described in the poetic treatises. This is the summary of all that has been said.

->The virtuous hall is filled with those worthy of the king’s majesty; it should be established with valiant heroes, ministers, and the splendor of fly-whisks.<-
->The assembly hall should be bow-shaped, with a throne-room of moderate height. **24**<-

<margin>Regarding the "fortunate seat" (throne) and the presence of the minister.</margin>

Regarding the assembly hall, it is said that it should be constructed and arranged according to the rituals described herein. As for the entrance into the hall, we shall describe that as well. In the **Thirteenth Chapter**, verse 80 of the poetic treatise <note>original: "Kavya"; likely referring to the root text this commentary is explaining</note>, [the rules are given]. In the **Nineteenth Chapter**, verse 80, the construction of the hall is detailed. One should establish it accordingly. In the beginning of the work, one should arrange it [the hall] thus; this application of the ritual should be contemplated by the wise scholars. **25**

# On the Procedure for Entering the Assembly

Now [the author] explains the procedure for entering the assembly hall <term>Sabha-pravesha-vidhi; the ritualized manner in which a monarch enters his court to begin official business</term>. The word **"Then"** <note>original: "tada"</note> refers to the lord, the king, who should step into the assembly. This means he should make his formal entrance into the gathering. The word for assembly used here, *sadah*, can be used in both the feminine and neuter genders. 

What should he do first? Right there, he should observe the duties related to the door-keepers. He should acknowledge the wise people and the heralds <term>Mangala-pathaka; professional bards or singers who recite auspicious verses to ensure a good beginning to the day's proceedings</term> who stand at his side. He faces a troop of elephants <term>Gaja-vraja; a ceremonial line or group of royal elephants</term> which are adorned with banners and flags. Amidst this gathering, the speed of the chariots is restrained. [Verse] 25.

> Then, facing the nearby troop of elephants adorned with banners, he performs his entrance into the assembly. While the heralds stand at his side singing praises, he should worship Ganesha, Vishnu, Shiva, the Sun, and the Goddess. He should remember the Guardians of the Directions and the Planets, and bow to the lords of the earth before taking his seat. [Verse] 26.

# On the Procedure for Ascending the Throne

Now he explains the procedure for ascending the "Auspicious Seat" <term>Bhadrasana; a ceremonial throne, often specifically blessed for royal use</term>. The phrase **"The Pillar"** refers to the King, the lord of the earth, who resides in this assembly on the royal throne. 

What must he do first? He should worship Ganesha <note>original: "Gajanana"; the elephant-headed god of beginnings</note>, Vishnu <note>original: "Hari"</note>, Shiva <note>original: "Hara"</note>, the Sun <note>original: "Hari"; here used to denote Surya, the sun god</note>, and the Goddess Lakshmi. Having done this, he must bow to the Brahmin scholars <term>Vipra; members of the priestly and intellectual class</term>. Furthermore, he should call to mind the Guardians of the Directions <term>Digishvara or Lokapala; the eight deities who protect the cardinal and ordinal points of the universe</term> and the celestial Planets <term>Graha; the nine celestial influencers in Indian cosmology</term>. He views these deities as the givers of boons and blessings.

# On the Duties upon Ascending the Throne

Now, according to the verses, he explains the duties to be performed once the King has ascended the throne. Having attained the status of the Leader of the Assembly <term>Sabha-pati; the lord or chairman of the royal court</term>, and having ascended the seat, he should maintain his composure among the astrologers <term>Daivavid; those who know the divine will through the stars</term> and the calculators <term>Ganaka; astronomers or mathematicians who calculate auspicious moments</term>. He should give land to the Twice-born <term>Dvija; members of the learned or priestly class</term> who stand before him. To the valiant men and the great warriors, he should present weapons for display and skill. To the royal priest, the messengers, and the cooks <note>original: "pachakebhyo"</note>, he should grant wealth. 

On this "Auspicious Seat" <term>Bhadrasana; a ritual throne designed to bring prosperity</term>, after honoring the astrologers and the deities, he grants land to the priests and <gloss>weapons</gloss> to the brave men. He should also give gifts to the teachers. To the heralds and messengers, the "Lord of the People" <term>Vishampati; a traditional title for a king as the protector of the subjects</term>, while seated on his throne, should grant what is required. All of this should be performed according to the various distinctions of the Vedas and in accordance with the deities of the lunar days <term>Tithi-devata; the specific gods governing each day of the lunar month</term>. [Verse] 28.

# On the Honoring of the Heralds

Now, regarding the "Awakening" <note>original: "Prabodha"</note>. Again, the Lord of the People, established upon his own throne, should give new garments <note>original: "nava-chivara"</note> to the bards and heralds <term>Vaitalika; court singers who praise the king and announce the time</term. In this manner, and by these means, the procedures mentioned in the various branches of the Vedas regarding the deities of the lunar days are to be carried out as established rules.
