# Now, the solar year is described

Now, the solar year <term>Suryavarsha</term> is described. Because the world is unchanging <note>original: jagat-avikāratvāt</note>, we look to the cause through the people. Now, regarding the months of the world, they are to be understood as starting with *Madhu* <note>another name for the month of Chaitra</note>, specifically from the beginning of the bright fortnight <term>Chaitra-sita-adi</term>. The limit of the month is the new moon <term>Amavasya</term>. In which period does this occur? It is in the same solar transit between the past and the coming years; this is the meaning. What is the measure of that month? To that, he says: the measure of the month is the time the Sun reaches and stays within a specific zodiacal field <term>Surya-kshetra</term>. If the Sun has moved upward, a lunar month <term>Chandramasa</term> is obtained. 74.

Now, he speaks of the fault of Jupiter <term>Guru-dosha</term> during the year’s festivals in countries such as Saurashtra <note>modern-day Gujarat peninsula</note>. In the solar year, the qualities of the Lord of Speech <term>Gishpati</term>, referring to Jupiter, are considered during his retrograde motion <term>vakra</term>. When the Sun is in the same position from the start of the bright half of Chaitra, that is always the path; that is the stated month. In the world, *Madhu* is the lunar month ending with the new moon. The measure of the month is from the middle of the Sun’s transit. 75.

In the region of Saurashtra and the divided land of Malava, the retrograde motion of Jupiter is not favorable for marriage <term>Vivaha</term>. Jupiter is not auspicious in the lands of Sindhu <note>the Indus region</note> and Maru <note>the desert region of Rajasthan</note> during religious vows. However, this prohibition should not be applied in other regions. 76. Favorable days are sought in marriage. Some are not favorable for auspicious ceremonies according to the words of Jupiter, as stated by the sage Galava. All these are considered here. Is the day of Jupiter <term>Jiva-vara</term> or Thursday favorable for marriage? In the land of Saurashtra and the divided land of Malava, it is so. The land of Malava, as divided by King Vikramarka <note>the legendary King Vikramaditya</note>, is famously known as Gurjara <note>Gujarat</note> in the ancient records <term>Purana</term>. Furthermore, in the lands of Sindhu and the Maru desert, these rules are followed, but they should not be applied in other lands. 77.

Now, according to the opinion of the Sages <term>Rishi-mata</term>, he meditates: "In marriage, even if Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation <note>original: nīcca-stha</note>, the days are not necessarily unfavorable." Retrograde motion can be favorable and auspicious for disputes, but in other auspicious ceremonies, they are not sought...

# Regarding the Prohibition of Marriage in the Magha Constellation

Now, the prohibition of marriage <term>vivāha-niṣedha</term> is described for the regions of Gauda and the lands surrounding the Godavari river when the Magha star is occupied. From the northern bank of the Godavari River up to the southern bank of the Bhagirathi <note>the Ganges</note>, and at the confluence of the Indus <term>Sindhu</term> at Prayag, marriage is not considered appropriate as long as Jupiter <term>Guru</term>—the "Lord of Speech"—resides in the zodiac sign of Leo <term>Siṃha Rāśi</term>. 

The specific meaning is this: as long as Jupiter remains in the Magha constellation <note>the first 13 degrees of Leo</note>, marriage is forbidden. Afterward, while still in the sign of Leo, marriage becomes auspicious. As it is said: "When Jupiter leaves Magha and enters the Phalguni constellation, it brings righteous conduct."

From the northern bank of the Godavari to the southern bank of the Bhagirathi, and at the confluence of the Indus, marriage is prohibited while Jupiter is in Leo. This is especially true while it remains in Magha. However, some say this fault is avoided in the regions of Gauda <note>modern Bengal</note>, Kalinga <note>modern Odisha</note>, Saurashtra <note>the Gujarat peninsula</note>, and the Kutch region. Even in the lands between the great rivers and the Gautami <note>another name for the Godavari</note>, the presence of Jupiter in Leo is considered a blemish. 25. When Jupiter is in the "Pot-Born" position <note>likely referring to specific degrees or the star Agastya</note>, a marriage performed then results in misfortune in the region of Bhadra-Gaja.

<insert>Resulting in the loss of good fortune and death, or death at the end.</insert> 

Furthermore, regarding Jupiter in Leo: when the Lord of Speech resides in the sign of the Lion, in all countries, it is said to bestow death upon the couple. This is according to the *Rajamartanda* <note>a famous 11th-century treatise on astrology and medicine attributed to King Bhoja</note>. 5. Regarding the specific faults of Jupiter and Venus <term>Guru-Śukra doṣa</term> in other regions: if a marriage is performed, it may cause the death of the bride <note>original: samprattā</note> who was given away. 22. Rama.

# Now, the Seven-Stick Diagram

Now begins the explanation of the Seven-Stick Diagram. In this system, there are twenty-eight "sticks" <note>original: "shalaakaa"; these are the horizontal and vertical lines that form the grid of the astrological chart</note> which describe the <term>Vedha</term> <note>literally "piercing"; an astrological phenomenon where a planet's position "strikes" or obstructs a specific lunar mansion, making it inauspicious</note>. 

Regarding the mnemonic "Kri-Sva-Pu" <note>Abbreviations for the lunar mansions Krittika, Svati, and Punarvasu</note>: In the context of a marriage ceremony, if a mansion is "pierced" by a <unclear>planet</unclear>, that mansion is not to be used. The remaining mansions are considered unfavorable if they are struck by malefic planets. However, if a mansion is "pierced" by a benefic planet, it is considered auspicious. But if it is "pierced" by a malefic... it results in the most difficult circumstances. In the case of <term>Vedha</term>, if the specific "feet" <note>quarters or divisions of a lunar mansion</note> of the mansion are marked by malefic planets, the result is inauspicious. 1.

---

In this marked diagram, what is the nature of the chart? It is said to represent the three worlds. This same principle is also read in the Five-Stick Diagram. The calculation of the twenty-seven or twenty-eight lines follows a specific order: the horizontal lines are drawn from the Northeast <note>original: "aishanya"; the direction associated with the deity Ishana (Shiva), considered the most sacred direction in Vedic architecture and astrology</note> to the end. One must include the twenty-eighth mansion, <term>Abhijit</term> <note>a "hidden" lunar mansion located between Utthara Ashadha and Shravana, often used in specific ritual calculations</note>, in this counting. This is how the complete diagram is formed.

# Regarding the Timing of Auspicious Alignments

<margin>Atritā <note>likely a reference to a specific school of thought or a sage name</note></margin>

On which day of the marriage? <margin>Note</margin>

Now, regarding the burning [of sins] and the purification of the land, the Lord <note>original: "Bhago"; referring to Bhaga, the solar deity who presides over the Phalguni constellations and represents fortune and marriage</note> spoke: "O Bhaga!" He stated that while the **Purva Phalgunis** <term>the "former" mansion, ruled by the god of death, Aryaman</term> were involved, it was for the daughter of **Janaka** <note>Sita, the heroine of the Ramayana</note> that the curse and the wealth of her marriage were determined. Because she possessed true strength <note>original: "sattva"</note>, she attained all perfection. For this reason, because of her attained strength, in the ritual cycle of the **Uttara Phalgunis**, the third step of the curse was reached. To remedy the curse on the daughter of Janaka, she gave herself to the wealth of the ritual. Thus, she attained the auspiciousness of marriage as spoken by Valmiki. Even if there were difficulties, they were overcome by her essential nature. For this reason, the **Uttara Bhadrapada** <term>another of the "Uttara" or "Latter" mansions</term> is also used.

This refers to the Great Soul, **Rama**, and the lordly nature of his speech. It is said that "Rama is the creator of the world." Regarding the destruction of the curse, we hear of the purification of those living in sin through the power of hearing <note>original: "shravana"; possibly a double-meaning referring to the Nakshatra Shravana, associated with hearing sacred texts</note>. if there is a "Unity of Fruit" <term>Phalaikata; a condition where various astrological factors harmonize to produce a single positive result</term> from the power of the **Tara** <term>the strength of the lunar mansion or star relative to the individual's birth star</term>, then the five-fold fruits of that star are counted.
In such a case, even what was previously forbidden may be performed in this marriage. This is the meaning. [11] Rama.

# The Characteristics of Rising Signs

Now, the author describes the characteristics of the rising signs <term>Udaya; the sign of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>. Rituals for house-building and marriage are considered auspicious when performed during all favorable rising signs and ascendants <term>Lagnas</term>. Under which specific rising signs is this the case? It is particularly favorable when signs such as Aries <note>original: "Mesha"</note> and Gemini <note>original: "Mithuna"</note> are rising, or when certain specific planetary alignments occur. Furthermore, what are the conditions for these risings? They should be free from planetary afflictions <term>Vedha; literally 'piercing', referring to an unfavorable astrological aspect</term>. When a movable ascendant <term>Chara Lagna; the zodiac signs Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term> and a movable division <term>Chara Lava</term> occur <gloss>the rising sign and its movable division</gloss> <insert>excluding marriages</insert> then this rule applies. In any ritual task, that which follows the prescribed authority is considered auspicious. [22] Furthermore, in marriage, the timing is auspicious based on both day and night ascendants.

---

All rising signs are considered auspicious for the Moon and planets, specifically those involving the signs of Aries, Cancer, and Gemini in this context. When these signs are free from afflictions and occur in a movable rising or a movable division, they follow the traditional measure of authority. [22] For the Sun and Moon, the learned experts <term>Visharadah; those skilled in the science of time</term> have calculated the portion of the day already passed. In the calculation of time for these ascendants, the measure for the night is stated as being triple that of the day. [23]

### Conflicts Arising from the Twilight Timing

For this reason, one must also understand the contradictions <note>original: "virodha"</note>. # The Specifics of the Cow-Dust Hour [55]

Now, he explains the distinction between the specific and non-specific qualities of the Cow-dust period <note>original: "Godhulika"; refers to the auspicious time at sunset when returning cattle kick up dust</note>. Those who dwell in the mountains—the mountain-folk—and the various groups of people who have come together in this Age of Conflict <note>original: "Kali Yuga"; the current cosmic age in Hindu chronology, characterized by a loss of spiritual clarity</note>, are addressed here. This general teaching is proclaimed for the Priests <term>Vipra: the Brahmin or priestly class</term>, the Warriors <term>Kshatriya: the ruling or military class</term>, and the Merchants <term>Vaishya: the trading and agricultural class</term> [55].

# The Distinction of Time and the Twilight Ascendant [56]

Now, he explains the discernment between the time-measure <term>Ghatika: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term> and the Cow-dust hour. In all lands, the ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> is established by the measure of time.

> For those living in the mountains, the cow-dust hour arises from the gathering of the herds. In this Age of Conflict, just as in the beginning, it is pure for the Priests and others [55]. In all lands, the ascendant is fixed by time; in all castes, those who are wise <note>original: "Kovida"</note> have spoken of the cow-dust hour as a jewel among times in this age [56]. This path is not described for the days of the autumn and rainy months; the ascendant is stated in the Circle of Stars <term>Bhagamandala: the zodiac or the celestial sphere</term> based on the knowledge of place and time [57].

Here, in this investigation, it is applicable to all castes—the Priests and all other colors <note>original: "Varna"; the four-fold social order</note>. The wise say that the Cow-dust hour is like a jewel among ascendants [56]. 

# The Time-Ascendant in Specific Months [57]

Now he speaks of the time-measure ascendant during the month of Kartika <note>October–November</note> and others. The learned ones <note>original: "Kritayah"</note> say that during the days of the months of Kartika, Margashirsha <note>November–December</note>, and Bhadrapada <note>August–September</note>, the desired time-measure is the ascendant. In these months, one should not wander from the path, for the Cow-dust hour in the circle of the zodiac is what brings success to auspicious works <note>original: "Mangala-karya"</note>, according to the proper rules of measurement.

# The Dissolution of Merit in the Cow-Dust Hour

Now, regarding the application of the **Cow-dust hour** <term>Godhulika: the auspicious twilight time when cows return home, raising dust</term> for those seeking service or returning home. Because of the respect shown to the customs of the people <note>original: "lokanam dharmam"</note>, as noted by the sage **Badarayana** <note>A name for the sage Vyasa, indicating that even the highest authorities acknowledge local custom</note>. 72.

# The Order of Marriage
## Discernment Regarding Family Traditions

For example: Regarding the prohibition of a **younger son’s marriage** <term>udvaha: marriage/wedding ceremony</term> when the **elder son** is still unmarried. Even when an elder brother is present, if a younger brother marries first, it is said that such a marriage "burns" the **family tradition** <term>Kuladharma: the specific religious and moral duties belonging to a particular lineage</term> and turns it to ashes.

For this reason, one should always follow **good conduct** <note>original: "sadachara" — the behavior of the virtuous</note> in selecting a groom. When an elder son exists, one should ensure that no resentment or anger arises by marrying the younger one first. 23.

### On the Birth of Twins
Now, the author discusses the "Discernment of Marriage" <note>original: "Udvaha-Viveka"</note> regarding the birth of **twins** <note>original: "yamalladi-prasava"</note> and similar cases, for all times and circumstances.

When a younger brother marries before the elder, it destroys the family merit. Therefore, in this world, such an act is deemed unworthy. When a suitable groom exists in the form of an elder son, no other should be chosen for marriage before him. 23.

However, a question arises regarding the birth of twins. When an **elder** and a **younger** are born at the same time, does the fault <note>original: "dosha" — a ritual or moral defect</note> of "marrying out of order" <note>the sin of the "Parivetta," or the younger brother who marries before the elder</note> still apply? In the case of a twin birth, the strict sequence might be viewed differently so that no fault is incurred. 24.

When a **twin birth** <note>original: "yugma-prasava"</note> occurs, one must not rely on mere guesswork. If the younger is married while the other remains, is there a fault for the elder's subsequent marriage? It is explained that in such a sequence, the family merit is not destroyed, because in a twin birth, the distinction of seniority is viewed through a different lens of "progeny sequence" <note>this refers to the Shastric debate on whether the first-born twin or the last-born twin is considered the elder</note>. Thus, the usual prohibition does not apply in the same way. 25.

# Now, the Purity of Garment Production is Described

Now, the author explains the purity required for the initial production of garments. On a **bright day** <note>original: "site'hani" - referring to Monday or Friday, which are considered 'white' or gentle days</note>, during the **bright fortnight** <note>the period of the waxing moon</note>, and under the influence of the **Varuna** constellation <note>the lunar mansion Shatabhisha</note>, the creation of a new garment should begin. This action brings about many successful results. On which days specifically? On Monday, Friday, Thursday, or Sunday. Regarding the constellations, the "short" or "light" <note>Kshipra/Laghu</note> constellations are preferred. Beginning with **Krittika** <term>Krittika: the 'Pleiades' lunar mansion, associated with fire and transformation</term> and the following nine, all these are considered under the lordship of the Divine. In these stars, when the weaver <term>Uvinda: a technical term for a weaver or the process of weaving</term> uses the **loom** <term>Vemakhya: literally 'that which is called the loom'</term>, the cloth produced is considered to have a copper-like <note>or radiant</note> quality. The cloth that comes from the **weaver's loom** <term>Uvinda-vemakhya</term> and is then worn, provides prosperity and success to the wearer. 4

---

In the **bright fortnight** and on the aforementioned days, the creation of new cloth should take place. For the cloth originating from the **weaver’s loom** <term>Uvinda-vemakhya-tariya</term>, there are specific rhythmic measures to be followed. 4. When the cloth is "released from the weaver" <term>Uvinda-mukta</term>, it is prepared and refined. When it is **ritually washed** <note>dhauta</note>, it brings about an auspicious state. The gods themselves acknowledge this as the primary method. The "weaver-union" <note>referring to the state of the cloth before it is purified from the loom's influence</note> is otherwise considered to be affected by defects. 5

---

Now, the author describes the suitability for wearing garments for those who are wise. It is said that for your wearing, the best garment is that which is **released from the weaver** <term>Uvinda-mukta-kriyam</term>. This refers to a cloth that has been **washed once** <note>original: "sakrid-dhautam"</note>. Once it has been rinsed a single time, it becomes firm and ready. In the language of the scholars, for any auspicious time or ceremony, such a garment should be worn to ensure the influence of the planets is favorable. For those who are highly learned, the second washing of the garment removes the "weaver-influence" <note>Uvinda-bhava</note> entirely, thus neutralizing the transition from the workshop to the ritual space.

<margin>4</margin>
<margin>The pacification of defects in the three [worlds/states]. 5.</margin>

# Now, the Auspicious Conditions for Wearing White Garments are Stated

Under the **light and swift** constellations <note>original: "Laghu"; a category of lunar mansions including Ashwini, Pushya, and Hasta known for providing quick results</note>, a man who wears a **white garment** <note>original: "shveta-vastra"</note> will find that it brings about the **attainment of all success**. On which days or under which planetary influences? Under the influence of **Venus** <note>original: "Shukra"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "Guru"</note> in the morning, the goal is achieved <gloss>attained</gloss>. The auspicious stars are **Ashvini**, **Hasta**, **Svati**, **Vishakha**, **Anuradha**, **Dhanishtha** <note>original: "Basave"</note>, **Punarvasu** <note>original: "Aditya-pu"</note>, **Pushya**, and **Revati**.

# Now, the Auspicious Conditions for Wearing Red Garments are Stated

Wearing a **red garment** <note>original: "rakta-vastra"</note> that is **crimson-hued** <note>original: "shona-nibha"</note> is considered highly auspicious and excellent. Under which conditions? It should be done when **Jupiter**, **Venus**, **Mars** <note>original: "Ara"</note>, or the **Sun** <note>original: "Ravi"</note> are the ruling planets. Among these, Jupiter and Venus are preferred. Regarding the stars, the two **Ashvini Kumars** <note>the twin celestial physicians who rule the first lunar mansion, Ashvini</note> are considered the best.

When the constellations are **light** <term>Laghu: swift-moving stars</term> and a man wears such a garment, he gains great peace. When the white-rayed planet <note>Venus</note> and Jupiter are present, it gives all success. 8. When one is in the presence of the crimson-colored light, wearing the garment is most auspicious. It should be done on the days of the **Moon** <note>Monday</note>, **Jupiter** <note>Thursday</note>, and **Venus** <note>Friday</note>. In the stars of **Revati**, **Ashvini**, and **Dhanishtha**, and when the Moon is in the friendship-forming star <term>Maitra-bha: the constellation Anuradha</term>, one should put on the garment. For **tawny** <note>brownish-orange</note> and **yellow garments**, let these rules be followed.

# On the Results of Timing for Special Garments and the Lunar Mansions

Now, the results regarding the timing for wearing garments made of hair or fur <note>original: "lomapara-su"</note> and the proper placement of items on the head are explained. This is auspicious when the completion of the ritual occurs under specific stars. The wearing of such items on the head <note>original: "shirsa-dharane"</note> is favorable when the Moon is in the constellation of **Hasta** <term>Hasta: the "Hand" constellation, associated with skill and grasping</term>, or during the triad of the **Vishakha** stars, or the triad of **Mrigashira**.

Under the pairing of the divine mothers, the constellations **Punarvasu** <term>Punarvasu: the "Return of the Light" constellation</term> and **Pushya** <term>Pushya: the "Nourishing" constellation, considered the most auspicious for spiritual and material works</term> are recommended. A fort <term>Durga: a fortified stronghold</term> is inauspicious for its lords if it is without a surrounding fortress wall. In a city, such a thing should never be, for it is by seeking refuge within these walls that kings rule upon the earth. In the direction of the gods <note>original: "vishvadevatara-ashayam," referring to the North-East or a specific auspicious compass point</note>, the boundary walls protect against enemies. 1

A difficult fort is one adorned with [defenses against] thieves and enemies, featuring <term>Kapi-shirsha: literally 'monkey-heads,' these are the shaped battlements or crenellations atop a rampart</term> and beautiful gateways. It should be decorated with various machines and watchtowers. 2 <margin>La</margin>

The moat <term>Parikha: a deep ditch or moat surrounding a fort</term> is like the very form of Time <note>original: "kala-rupini," implying it is as unavoidable and deadly as death or time itself</note>, terrifying to the enemy. Without the three-fold strength of the battlements and the heights of the gateways, the city lacks its proper pride. 3

The fort should be occupied by brave soldiers, well-equipped with weapons such as clubs, maces, snares, spears, and javelins, ready to engage in the waves of battle. 4 <margin>Ke Dra</margin>

First is the **Earth Fortress** <note>original: "Manmayam-kota," a fort made of mud or rammed earth</note>; the **Water Fortress** is second. Third is the **Village Fortress**, and fourth is the **Hill Fortress** found in the mountains. 5

The fifth is the **Wind Fortress** <note>original: "Pavanarohe," likely referring to a fort built on high, windy plateaus or a "Desert Fort" where wind is a barrier</note>; the sixth is the **Excellent Fortress**; and the seventh is known as the **Uneven-Ground Fortress**, along with others of that nature. 6

Thus, in a town or city, the appropriate location [for the king's residence] is determined by one's own zodiac sign <term>Sva-rashi: the astrological sign of the king or the city's founding</term>; other locations would be too distant or unsuitable. Therefore, I shall now describe the determination and the specific arrangement for the construction of the ramparts, the city, and the great gates, as told to the Master. 1

### Now he describes the purification of the Ascendant for entering a place

Regarding the phrase **"In a fixed [sign]"**: Now he describes the auspicious timing for entering a newly elevated city. It should occur in a **Fixed Sign** <term>Sthira-rashi: Signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and permanence</term>. What kind of fixed sign? One that is "purified" <note>original: "shuddhi"</note>.

Furthermore, he mentions the **Angular Houses** <term>Kendra: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the "pillars" of life</term> and the **Fifth House** <term>Dhi: The house of intellect and children</term>. These should be occupied by **Benefics** <term>Shubha: Auspicious planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a waxing Moon</term>.

<margin>Strength</margin>

The **Ninth House** <note>the house of fortune and merit</note> should also be well-placed. In this configuration, where are the **Malefics** <term>Khala or Krura: "Cruel" planets like Mars or Saturn</term> located? They should be in the **Sixth** <note>house of enemies/debts</note>, the **Third** <note>house of courage</note>, and the **Eleventh** <note>house of gains</note>. Furthermore, the entry should happen when the **Moon** <note>original: "Vidhu"</note> has **full digits** <term>Adhikala: A waxing or full moon, signifying increasing prosperity</term>. Again, with whom? With the lords of the current planetary period <note>Dasha</note> and the lord of the birth sign being in favorable positions.

### Now he describes the nature of the entry and sovereignty

Regarding the entry: the King, having been seated within the city as previously established, should be adorned with garments according to divine ritual. He should then present offerings to the priest. In the <gloss>fodder</gloss> fields <note>original: "yavase"; likely referring to the ritual feeding of livestock or land consecration</note>, he should give to the sun-god Rahu <note>a propitiatory offering to the shadow planet Rahu to avert misfortune</note>. Again, in the assembly of the twice-born <term>Dvija: "Twice-born," referring to the three upper classes of Vedic society, here specifically the Brahmins</term>, he should listen to the recitation of the Vedas. He should satisfy the <gloss>bards</gloss> and panegyrists <note>original: "vandi-magadhan"</note> with gifts of clothing. Furthermore, he should satisfy the women and the common folk with gifts of food. 10. Thus ends the fifteenth [chapter] of the Illustrious Go... 15.

### Now, after the completion of the city walls, follows the completion of the house

Now begins the determination for the commencement of the house. The Householder stage <term>Garhasthyam: The second stage of life in the Hindu system, focused on family, career, and social duty</term> is established because, among the four stages of life, the householder stage is the most significant.

For the sake of great fame, the householder stage is the <gloss>best</gloss> among the stages of life. Through the performance of one’s duties, one becomes a self-controlled person. ### On the Pacification of Directional Defects in House Construction

Now, regarding the construction of a house, for the sake of pacifying the defects of direction <term>Dig-dosha-shanti: Rituals or architectural adjustments to neutralize negative energy from improper orientation</term>, we consider the classes <term>Varna: The four social orders—Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra</term> beginning with the Brahmins, and the lunar mansions beginning with Ashvini. In the world, in the various positions of the planetary houses, the signs such as Taurus <note>original: "Vrusha"</note> are assigned. In the direction of Indra <note>the East</note>, a house for these men is auspicious. Likewise, in the direction of the Giver of Wealth <note>Kubera, the North</note>, a triangular house is auspicious. In the direction of Varuna <note>the West</note>, a house for the Vaishyas <note>the merchant class</note> is auspicious. In the direction of Yama <note>the South</note>, a house for the Shudras <note>the laborer class</note> is auspicious. Again, in the direction of Capricorn <note>original: "Makara"</note>, a house for those of the Capricorn sign is auspicious. Furthermore, in the direction of the lineage of Ikshvaku <note>a legendary royal solar dynasty</note>, wherever the village is centered, a house facing that direction is preferred. 1.

Now he speaks of the protection and compatibility of the directions through the "Limb of the Serpent" <term>Naganga: A technical Vastu calculation used to determine the compatibility between a person and a location</term>. For cities and men, a "Serpent" house is not best. If there is friction <note>original: "karkasa"</note>, it leads to another birth <note>unlucky or fatal results</note> in the eastern direction.

> Taurus and its enemies; the master of the forest and the dog; the three corners and the truth; in the forest of mixed stars and classes, the directions are auspicious. In the grace of the sign of Capricorn, in the middle of the directions. 2. By the "Limb of the Serpent," the friendship between the man and the house is determined; through the form of the god Hari, one is protected. The friction leads to another birth for kings; before the gods and Yama, it protects the men. 3.

Regarding the "Enemy of the Serpent" <note>likely referring to specific astrological combinations that negate "Naga" defects</note> and the constellations and signs: here the five best are the signs of Taurus, Leo, Gemini, and Capricorn. What is the meaning? For a man in the eastern direction, a house should not be in the sign of Scorpio <note>original: "Vrischika"</note>. Furthermore, for a man in the sign of Capricorn <note>original: "Mruga"</note>, in the direction of Yama [South], and again with the sign of Pisces <note>original: "Meena"</note>, there is delight. Thus, for the sign of Capricorn in the Northeast <note>original: "Ishanya"</note>; with Gemini <note>original: "Mithuna"</note> again; with the nine [signs]; with Sagittarius <note>original: "Dhanu"</note> in the West; again with the sign of Capricorn in the Northwest <note>original: "Vayavya"</note>; again with Aries <note>original: "Mesha"</note> in the North; again with the fierce sign of Aquarius <note>original: "Kumbha"</note> in the Northeast. In these cases, there is the wrath of Saturn <note>original: "Shani-prakobha"</note>.

### On the Alignment of Directions, Cities, and Zodiac Signs

Now, regarding the combination of the direction, the city, and the zodiac signs, to ensure an auspicious outcome for the house: if the signs are **Pisces** <note>original: "Meena"</note>, **Scorpio** <note>original: "Ali"</note>, or **Leo** <note>original: "Simha"</note>, the man should be East-facing <note>original: "Pragasya"</note>, looking toward the sunrise. <margin>n</margin>
When **Taurus** <note>original: "Vrisha"</note>, **Capricorn** <note>original: "Makara"</note>, or **Virgo** <note>original: "Kanya"</note> are the established signs, he is designated as West-facing <note>original: "Paschadva"</note>. <margin>Furthermore, facing the Southern direction is connected to certain signs</margin>
When the signs are **Gemini** <note>original: "Mithuna"</note>, **Libra** <note>original: "Tula"</note>, or **Sagittarius** <note>original: "Dhanu"</note>, he is likewise proclaimed to be West-facing <note>Note: There appears to be a variation or scribal error here, as these are typically associated with the South in other systems</note>.

### On the Auspicious Timing for Commencing Construction

Now, regarding the commencement of a house: when the month, its presiding lord, and the lunar mansion are in a favorable conjunction, the start of work yields excellent results and brings great prosperity. <note>original: "bhṛśa-phala-kṛt"</note> Even if the month falls during the **Southern Transit of the Sun** <note>original: "Dakshinayana," typically considered less auspicious for new beginnings</note>, or specifically when the month has returned to the **Northern Transit** <note>original: "Udati-gayana"</note>, entering the new house is still appropriate and permissible. <meta>Catchword: sho</meta>
Because the deities governing the foundation-laying <note>original: "Chatana"</note> and those governing the housewarming <note>original: "Praveshana"</note> are distinct, the auspicious moments <note>original: "Muhurtas"</note> for these two acts are also different. What is the nature of a flawed start? One occurring on "empty" lunar days <note>original: "Rikta-tithis," the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of a lunar fortnight</note>, or under unlucky planetary alignments and wicked conjunctions. Such a commencement is said to be struck by the "fallen rule" <note>original: "vidhir-bhruśapāta"</note> and must be avoided.

---

-> Even when the month is in the Southern Transit, starting construction can yield <-
-> excellent results; however, one must distinguish between foundation-laying and <-
-> housewarming, as their presiding deities and rituals differ. 8. When the Sun <-
-> is in Leo or Capricorn, or in Aquarius or Cancer, the face of the time-spirit <-
-> looks toward the North-East. In Taurus, Libra, or Scorpio, the result is <-
-> a rain of fruit; however, one must watch the direction of the Lord of Death. 9. <-

---

8. The text now explains the orientation of the planets and the directions they face. When the **Sun** <note>original: "Bhanu"</note> is in **Leo** <note>original: "Kesari"</note>—the solar transition into Leo—or in **Capricorn** <note>original: "Mriga"</note>—the solar transition into Capricorn—and similarly when the Sun is in **Aquarius** <note>original: "Kumbha"</note> or **Cancer** <note>original: "Karka"</note>, the "face" is said to be toward the **North-East** <note>original: "Ishana"</note>. Furthermore, the "face" is directed toward the West <note>original: "Pashchima"</note> in other specific alignments. When the Sun transitions into **Taurus** <note>original: "Gau"</note>, **Libra** <note>original: "Nrka"</note>, or **Scorpio** <note>original: "Bhramara"</note>, and in **Aries** <note>original: "Mesha"</note>, the influence of the Moon and Sun together creates a "rain of results" <note>meaning a bounty of success</note>. However, one must be mindful of the direction where the **Lord of Death** <note>original: "Kinasha," a name for Yama</note> sleeps, specifically toward the North-East in these configurations. 7.

In this work, the author states the standard measurement of a month: <gloss>In this way</gloss> regarding the "month," as it is measured by the duration between two **New Moons** <note>original: "darsha-yugala-kalena"</note>, it follows that a "Darshika" <note>New-Moon-ending or Amanta</note> month is defined by the period between two consecutive **New Moon days** <note>original: "Amavasya"</note>. This lunar month is established as authoritative for planetary calculations and for the **construction of dwellings** <note>original: "nilaya-kritau"</note>; this measure of time is declared to be standard in all lands and regions.

---

-> A month is the interval between two New Moons; <-
-> it is established as authoritative for construction everywhere, <-
-> especially in the lands between the River of Heaven and the daughter of Kalinda. <-

---

This is the case in the regions of the **Ganga** <note>referred to here as "Suradhuni," the River of the Gods</note> and the **Yamuna** <note>referred to as "Kalindaja," the daughter of Mount Kalinda</note>. In the territories situated between these two rivers, the calculation follows the Moon <note>original: "Vidhu"</note>. Specifically, it concerns the "Paurnimasika" month <note>the Purnimanta system, where the month ends on the Full Moon</note>, where the month is reckoned by the cycle of the Moon and the Full Moon day occurs as the midpoint or defining transition. 8

<note>The text highlights a geographic distinction in Vedic time-keeping: the Amanta system (New Moon to New Moon) and the Purnimanta system (Full Moon to Full Moon), noting their specific applications in the sacred geography of the Indo-Gangetic plain.</note>

# Now, he explains the Cycle of Directions, Doors, and Mansions

Now, he explains the **Cycle of Directions, Doors, and Mansions** <note>original: "dig-dvara-bha-chakra"; a specialized diagram used in Vastu Shastra to determine the auspicious placement of doors relative to the lunar mansions</note> starting with "Svamiti." In the **Moon-Night Cycle** <note>original: "indunishota-chakra"</note> or the **House Cycle**, one begins from the **East** <note>original: "prachya"</note>. From the **Fire-star** <note>original: "anala-bha," referring to the Krittika nakshatra or the Pleiades</note>, one should count by groups of seven. One should always desire the commencement of the house construction under the auspicious signs mentioned. He who begins when the stars are favorable towards the owner—peaceful and medicinal—will find the beginning of the doors to be properly joined. 12

# On the Defects of Dwellings and the Timing of Plastering

Now, he explains the defects to be observed in thatched houses <note>original: "darmyadi"; referring to houses made of grass or wood</note> and others. He states that one should not move toward or face the Sun <note>original: "tapakara"; literally 'the heat-maker'</note> with excessive speed. In the traditional sciences, it is taught that one should not stay in a place where the sun's rays are obstructed or hidden. In a **leaf-hut** <note>original: "parna-kuta"; a simple thatched cottage</note> or similar dwelling, the position of the Sun must be carefully observed. If the Sun is visible through the gaps of the thatched roof, it is considered a defect that brings ill fortune. In a house constructed of **bricks** <note>original: "ishtaka"</note> or **clods of earth** <note>original: "mrit-pinda"</note>, the primary focus should be on the proper alignment of the structure. 24 Now, regarding brick-built houses:

->the Sun’s rays within a thatched cottage are undesirable.<-
->In a bright house of earth, the alignment must be precise. 25<-

->in the months of Ashvin and others, the plastering of the hall should be done,<-
->including the upper floors and the pillars. 17<-

He then discusses the purity and the **plastering** <note>original: "lepa"</note> of the assembly hall. For a dwelling made of stone or refined wood, or a two-story house, or one made specifically of timber, he describes the first application of plaster and the cleaning of the hall. He asks: what is the use of a house without proper coating? The construction is made firm with a mixture of earth and water. The auspicious stars for this are the "Steady Ones": the **Deer’s Head** <note>original: "Mriga" / Mrigashirsha</note>, the **Wealthy One** <note>original: "Revati"</note>, the **Bright One** <note>original: "Chitra"</note>, and the **Friend** <note>original: "Mitra" / Anuradha</note>. 3

# Chi Gu

<header>Chi Gu</header>

At the time of the **Ascendant** <note>original: "udaye"; the rising sign at the moment of birth</note>, if a planet is in its **exalted position** <note>original: "socca-pada-śrī"; literally 'the glory of the high place'</note>, it is accompanied by the prosperity of that high station. This means the planet is situated in **Pisces** <note>original: "mīnastha"</note>. When the **Poet** <note>original: "kavi"; a common name for the planet Venus</note> is thus situated in the heart of the Ascendant, or if the immortal gods—those who partake in nectar—bestow their influence through the divine speech of the **Teacher** <note>original: "guru"; the planet Jupiter</note>, and if he is possessed of wealth and situated in the **royal house** <note>original: "nṛpa-bhāva"</note> in the sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "karkasthā"</note>, specific results follow. Or, if **Saturn** <note>original: "yamaḥ/śaniḥ"</note>—the one of steady gait—is positioned in a state of protection and service, then the five-fold knowledge of **Venus** <note>original: "śukra"</note>, **Jupiter**, and **Saturn** in the **decan** <note>original: "dṛkkāṇaka"; a 10-degree divisional chart</note> of the family lineage, placed in their **own houses** <note>original: "svagṛhe"</note>, establishes the continuity of the family line itself. 25. Now, regarding the house of the **mother** <note>original: "mātṛ-bhāriṇyā"; likely referring to the 4th house</note> or one's own home, in the path of the wind and the sky, and in the performance of sacrifices—going and coming—these are established by the **restraints** <note>original: "nigrahaistaiḥ"; referring to the restrictive or controlling aspect of the planets</note> which have completed their intended purpose.

At the rising, the Poet <note>Venus</note> appears in his exalted glory. The one who partakes in nectar <note>Jupiter</note>, the lord of wealth, creates a prosperous state. When situated in the family lineage, in the role of the family-builder, he possesses a steady and bold gait. 29. Residing in his own house, or in his exaltation, he stays for a vast amount of time. Through the works and desires created by Venus in the **fifth house** <note>original: "pañcamasya śukra-kṛta"; the house of creativity, children, and intellect</note>... 17. The **Heir Apparent** <note>original: "yuvarāja"; likely referring to Mercury or a secondary planetary influence</note> goes to the further portion, where a single intoxicating lord of the winds is the master. In this arrangement, he approaches passion through the path of the true time. 18.

<margin>By these five planetary restraints, it is said that whenever this occurs, these conflicts should be understood. In that place, one reads the position of the "Doer" <note>the primary planet acting in the chart</note> in his own house and marks the time. If it is thus, the path from the other side is demonstrated; this knowledge of "other-pleasure" is mine. 29.</margin>

In the position of the "Doer" in his own house, for a vast and abundant time, what is heard of the work performed? If there is effort in the past, what is heard of the wind?
In one's own house, or in an **exalted station** <note>original: "ucca-sthāne"</note>, or in the seventh house, or in the **house of a friend** <note>original: "mitra-gṛhe"</note>, these are the connections of one's own house and day. When planets have gone to the **six stations** <note>original: "ṣaṭ-sthāneṣu"; often referring to the difficult 6th, 8th, and 12th houses</note>, there is a loss of fame. Thus, if a planet is in its own house or station but [afflicted], it can lead to great **poverty** <note>original: "dāridryaṃ"</note>. 20. Just as the two lords, Jupiter and Venus, rule the groups of twenty, so too do Jupiter, Venus, Mars, and Saturn move through the various cycles...

Now he states the exception regarding the interior of the house near the **Shalini** <note>original: "shālini"; likely referring to a specific style of house or a hall with pillars</note>. # On the Results of Trees and Other Features Near the Dwelling

Now he states the results of trees and other features located near the house. The phrase **"Half..."** refers to the three types of foundations or stones known as **Vedha** <term>Vedha</term> <note>literally "piercing"; refers to obstructions such as a tree or a pillar that aligns awkwardly with the main door</note>. If these are present in the dwelling, they cause distress. If situated in the middle, they must be avoided. A dwelling that lacks proper cover or residing space is termed a **Kuya** <note>a "bad" or "defective" house</note>. Furthermore, in villages that are honored or well-established, one should only consider those trees that are **Gṛha-shasta** <gloss>auspicious for the house</gloss>. By the combination of these auspicious trees, those that grow nearby are considered beneficial to the householder. 33

Now he describes the auspicious and inauspicious forms of trees based on their classification. A dwelling should be built separately; it is not considered auspicious otherwise. Even if a site is generally honored, for the sake of the inhabitants, one should use trees like the **Shala** <note>Sal tree, Shorea robusta</note> only if they are healthy and well-placed. 33 Regarding the **Shala** <note>house or hall</note>, if there is a waterfall or if there are sapless trees like the **Tala** <note>Palm tree</note> or black varieties... in a place where people reside, a **Prasada** <term>Prasada</term> <note>a temple or a multi-storied mansion</note> is not auspicious if it is built on ground that is unsuitable. # On the Faults Occurring at the Start of Construction Regarding the Measurement Cord and Stakes

**Now, at the commencement of building the house, he describes the faults regarding the breaking of the measurement cord and the foundation stake, saying "Know..."** 

When opening the ground for the hall, if during the laying of the measurement cord <term>Sūtra-pāta</term> <note>the ritual act of stretching a cord to mark the house's dimensions</note> the cord should break, or if a knot forms, or if it is cut, then the builder or the householder will surely suffer affliction. In the excavated area, if a foundation stake <term>Kīla</term> <note>a wooden peg driven into the ground to mark vital points of the Vastu Purusha, the spirit of the site</note> is broken, it leads to disease. If the stake remains submerged or stuck in the earth, then there will be surprises or anxiety regarding one's children. 32

<margin>
If auspicious signs are observed, success is attained; he expands upon this in detail. 37
</margin>

In the preparation of the hall, during the laying of the cord, a break or a knot affects the builder in the same way. A broken stake or one submerged in the earth in the excavated area may signify death or a shocking event. 39 In the excavated area, one should look at the leveled ground to see if there are stones, hair, charcoal, bones, or leather. If such things are found, or if something white appears, it foretells a fear of the king <term>Rāja-bhīti</term> <note>historically, this refers to legal troubles, fines, or punishment from the state authorities</note>. However, if auspicious things are seen, it brings about success. 37

***

**He describes the results of objects seen during excavation**

If, while the ground is being dug, the wise practitioner <gloss>the learned architect or priest</gloss> first sees stones, hair, charcoal, bones, or leather, then there is a fear of the king [government]. These objects are considered impurities within the site.

Afterward, when the sun is in its Northern Transit, the construction of the house in the northern direction should be performed. 38

# The Permutation of House Types and the Sixteen Variations

**Now, he demonstrates the permutation <term>Prastara</term>** <note>original: "prastāra"; a mathematical method of listing all possible combinations of long and short units</note>: A wise person should write out the primary forms <term>Rupakas</term> <note>original: "rūpakān"</note> which are unmeasured by the previous instruments. One should write the long syllables <term>Guru</term> <note>original: "gurūn"</note> until the end of the calculation <gloss>until</gloss> all are completed. Then, below the first one, place a short syllable <term>Laghu</term> <note>original: "laghum" or "laghu"</note>; then, in the preceding spaces, place long syllables. This <margin>until</margin> process should be repeated <gloss>all</gloss> as long as the method requires. Since the feet are joined at the beginning, the final long syllables are replaced with short ones below. Thus, repeating the process for the remainder of the calculation. 41. Through the method of doubling the long syllables, the forms are produced. Thus the sequence proceeds. 42.

**Now, he demonstrates the placement of the short measure:** Always, one should write the short syllables <note>original: "laghu"</note> in their designated places. Following the calculation, place the short syllables below the long ones for the primary forms. Behind the short syllables, one should place a long syllable until the process is complete. 43. From the seat of the navel and so on, the numbers of the short syllables are counted in their places. This has been called the "set of ten" by the wise. 44. The drawing of lines should be pleasing to the mind. Even in harsh or difficult situations, these calculations do not fail. 45. In the "Victory" <term>Vijaya</term> <note>original: "vijaya"; the name of a specific auspicious house type</note> category, there are sixteen variations. These are designated by their beautiful names, and the result is said to be consistent with the name of the object. 46.

---

<margin>Name</margin>
The measure is said to be twofold. From the consideration of the house <note>original: "sadana"</note>, the measure of the first direction is determined as the left side. It is settled by those who know the eighty-three variations of the householder. 45. **Now, he speaks of the sixteen heavy names:** In the "Victory" category <note>original: "vijaya"</note>, there is a pair of six beautiful and similar types. These sixteen variations of the beginning of the site are explained. For the master of the house, the results are said to be consistent with the names, such as "Success" and the others. 48.

### On the Directional Movement and Broken Foundations

Now, he explains the movement through the directions when a foundation is broken: If the <term>foundation is broken</term> <note>original: "bhinnamūla"; refers to a structural disruption or a non-aligned base in the site plan</note> in **Yama’s portion** <note>original: "dharmarājāṃśe"; Yama, the Lord of Justice, is the directional deity of the South</note>, one should enter from the front in the southern direction, or <unclear>3</unclear> in the **Western direction** <note>original: "vāruṇyāṃ"; Varuna is the deity of the West</note> when the foundation is broken there. In the portion of the **North** <note>original: "udag-aṃśa"; Udag or Somya refers to the Northern direction</note>, if the foundation is broken, one should enter accordingly. Furthermore, for the Sun and other planets situated in the South, the residential portions should be determined starting from the foundation. Again, in this context, the door should be desired in the direction of the presiding planets. 48 Or rather:

He states that a door should never be placed in the corners. Even with the presence of a hundred **benefic planets**, there is no place for a door in the **corner** <note>original: "koṇādau"</note>. Why is this?

### Now, Concerning the Timing and Constellations for Fixing Door Timbers

Now, we shall write clearly regarding the constellations and other factors for the fixing of the door timbers <note>original: "shodha-daru-mochana"; the ritualized act of preparing or installing the wooden frame</note>. One should establish the auspicious timing. The Sun <note>original: "Kesarka"</note>, Jupiter <note>original: "Dhisana"</note>, and Venus are favorable. The auspicious lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras</term> include Pushya, Punarvasu <note>original: "Aditi"</note>, Anuradha <note>original: "Maitra"</note>, Rohini, Vishakha, and Swati <note>original: "Vayu"</note>. Also, Dhanishtha <note>original: "Vasu"</note>, Revati <note>original: "Paushna"</note>, and Ashvini <note>original: "Pratara"</note>. The Sun <note>original: "Tarani"</note>, Jupiter <note>original: "Dhisana"</note>, and Venus <note>original: "Kavya"</note> are the planets to be considered. For the crushing of obstacles, these should be utilized when free from "cruel combinations" <note>original: "krura-yoga"</note>. One should proceed during a stable Ascendant <note>original: "sthira-lagne"</note> when the "King’s Strength" <term>Raja-virya</term> <note>a specific potent astrological state of a planet</note> and the strength of the Moon are present. 58. Now, regarding the conclusion, the wise have accepted this method for halls and houses.

When Jupiter <note>original: "Dhisana"</note> is in the Ascendant, and the Moon is in Aries or other signs, with the influence of the Sun, Anuradha, Chitra, or other constellations, it is auspicious. Under the gaze of Mercury <note>original: "Soumya"</note>, one should perform the fixing of the timbers. When Jupiter, the Sun, and Venus are in the proper positions, and the "Lord of the Night" <note>the Moon</note> is favorable along with the King’s Strength, success is assured. 59. This procedure for houses, water-stalls <term>Prapa</term>, and other structures is the same as that used for stables <note>original: "mandura"</note>, elephant-stables <note>original: "varana-gehe"</note>, and temples <note>original: "devakula"</note>. The purification of the knowledge regarding the origins of the wood has thus been declared. 60. One should consult the teachings of Jupiter and others, but as for the epics such as the Ramayana and the Mahabharata... one should be careful in their application here.

<margin>Thus, the sixth section has been told.</margin>

Now, regarding the remaining designations once known, one should again proceed with the work of the buildings, such as hermitages <note>original: "ashrama"</note>, monasteries <note>original: "muni-sthane"</note>, or temples for Shiva <note>original: "Hara"</note>. Whether it be a stable for horses <note>original: "vaji-shala"</note>, an elephant stable, a cow-shed, a temple, or a water-stall, the same rules for the wood apply. These locations have been declared as requiring specific observation. 61. Now, he prohibits certain things regarding the house: in a residence, one should avoid depicting the themes of the Ramayana and the Great Bharata <note>the Mahabharata</note>. Specifically, the sequences involving the wars of the Ramayana and the Bharata should not be used in domestic settings <note>likely due to the belief that depicting conflict brings discord to a home</note>.

Now, the ritual work for **divine houses** <note>original: "devagṛha"; refers to temples or family shrines</note> and similar structures is considered pure in the month of Shravana <note>a summer month in the Hindu calendar, roughly July-August, associated with the monsoon and the god Shiva</note>. In the excellence of the temple, the construction of the residence should begin. The stars for beginning a house are generally auspicious. What are they? The stars of the Sun <note>original: "āditya"; referring to the star Punarvasu</note>, Punarvasu, the Nasatyas <note>original: "nāsatya"; referring to the star Ashvini</note>, Hasta, and Shravana. When Venus, the Sun, Punarvasu, and Ashvini are positioned favorably, they are considered to have shared influence.

Now, regarding the purification of rituals for **animal shelters** and similar structures, it is always appropriate to build a water-shed <note>term: <term>prapā</term> (a place for distributing free drinking water to travelers)</note> and a water-hall. In the three sets of three stars mentioned.

### Now, regarding the entry into the house and the effects of fierce and other lunar mansions

**Regarding the fierce stars:** In all various types of royal architectural layouts <note>original: "rājasanniveśana"; refers to the specific floor plans or structural arrangements designated for nobility or public buildings</note>, if one enters the house during a fierce lunar mansion <term>Ugra Nakshatra</term> <note>a category of stars including Bharani, Magha, Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada, considered harsh or cruel</note>, it leads to the total destruction of the inhabitants. It is said that the King's son, the Prince, will meet his death. With mixed lunar mansions <note>original: "mishra"; stars with combined qualities</note>, especially with Krittika <note>the Pleiades; a star associated with the fire god Agni</note>, there is a risk that the building will be destroyed by fire. 10.

Now, regarding the specific times for entry: The time for entry into the house is explained based on which lunar mansions have been completed or are currently active. This refers to the specific day the stars are positioned. In other cases, whether on specific days of the week or during particular times...

---

Under a fierce star, the King passes away; likewise, the King's son or the Princess. Under mixed stars, specifically Krittika, fire may break out in all varieties of royal dwellings. 10. Entry should not be made during the prohibited times or on a day of bad weather <note>original: "durdina"; literally "bad day," usually referring to dark, rainy, or cloudy weather that obscures the sun and stars</note>. However, if there are good omens <note>term: <term>sallakshana</term></note>, even if moving in reverse order, they may act as the cause for a successful entry. 11. 

The Yogini <note>a mystical energy or deity that moves through the directions of the compass on different lunar days; one should not face it when traveling or entering a house</note> should not be at the back or to the side of the person entering. If the Yogini is facing the person or positioned to the side, she is considered a "separated" <note>original: "viyoginī"</note> energy. One is free of this when the Yogini has completed her movement. When one must go to that specific house, the entry ritual is performed. If the house is a "Suta" house <note>a place where a birth has recently occurred</note>, or if there is a death, a patient, or if the house is primarily made of wood, the entry ritual must be handled with great care regarding these conjunctions. 22.

Regarding the phrase **"According to time..."**: Following the flow of the sun’s rays <note>original: "āditeusekānusāreṇa"; likely referring to the solar influence on the timing</note>, if a man makes his entry into the house courtyard when the planetary alignment is impure, his movement becomes a "path of the dead" <term>Pretagati</term> <note>a movement toward death or ill-fortune</note>; essentially, death will occur. Furthermore, if the entry occurs under a malefic star or a "thunderbolt" star <note>original: "aśanibhe"; stars associated with harsh electrical or sudden destructive energy</note> while in the physical layout, it leads to the destruction of life, the enmity of women, and such outcomes as would prevent any prosperity. On an "empty" day <term>Riktā</term> <note>the 4th, 9th, and 14th lunar days, usually avoided for new beginnings</note>, if the royal layout is entered under these conditions, it brings obstacles; one does not achieve lordship over the layout or their kin.

### The Procedure for House Entry

Now, the author describes the method for entering the house, beginning with the word **"Having performed..."**: A person of right mind <margin>Entering</margin> should enter the house through a door that is cleared and adorned with a festoon <term>Torana</term> <note>a decorative archway made of leaves or flowers used in Indian rituals</note>. How should one enter? By placing the Sun <gloss>the sun</gloss> on the left, and then moving forward.

-> At a time when the layout is unfavorable, entering leads to a path of death; under malefic influences in the royal circle, one meets with destruction. 23. <-

-> Having performed the ritual, with the left side positioned toward the sun, a man with a pure mind should enter the house, which is decorated with festoons and accompanied by the sounds of various musical instruments and auspicious songs. 24. <-

-> After entering, one should then worship the God who resides in the house <note>the Vāstu Puruṣa or presiding deity of the structure</note>, the Master, and the cows with fragrant pastes and various garments. Having invited the learned priests and the craftsmen, as well as the poor who have arrived, one should satisfy them with gifts. 25. <-

The text explains: "With the left side toward the sun" means using the ritual method of positioning. What kind of man? One who is "pure-minded," meaning his body and mind are purified. 27.

Next, the actions to be performed after entering the house are described, starting with **"After entering..."** <gloss>Entering</gloss>. The Master—the owner of the house—having entered the dwelling, should worship the deity of the house and the Guru with cows, gold, and fine garments. He should lead the "vessels" <note>original: "pavitra"; refers to the priests or the consecrated water</note> through the expert head priest. Then, he should worship the craftsmen <term>Shilpi</term> <note>the architects, masons, and laborers who built the house</note> and likewise honor the poor and the travelers who have gathered there with groups of gifts. 29.

### The Auspicious Placement of Household Goods

Now, the author speaks regarding the purification of placing goods within the house, beginning with the word **"Placement"** <note>original: "nikṣepa"</note>. A wise man should place all the household equipment <term>Upaskara</term> <note>refers to domestic utility items, furniture, and tools</note> in a house that is well-maintained and pleasing to the eye. He explains the specific items: the rows of large water-storage jars <term>Aliñjara</term>, the canopies <term>Vitāna</term>, the altars or chariots, the granaries and storehouses <term>Koṣṭha</term>, the grain-chests <term>Dhānyakośa</term>, and the placement of the couches <term>Talpa</term> and the kitchen <term>Mahānasa</term>. 

In which lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras</term> should these be placed? By these three: **Puṣya** <note>The "Nourishing" star</note>, the two **Aśvinīs** <note>original: "nāsatyam"; the twin physicians of the gods</note>, **Hasta** <note>The "Hand" star</note>, and **Śravaṇa** <note>The "Ear" star</note>. These are considered "fixed" or steady stars, and are suitable for this purpose. 

Next, he speaks of the purification regarding the acquisition or making of these household goods. One should not prepare or bring in the entirety of the household materials on the "New Moon" day <term>Darśa</term> or the "Empty" lunar days <term>Riktā</term> <note>The 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar fortnight, considered hollow or unlucky for new beginnings</note>. He also mentions specific astrological combinations <note>original: "ū-pu-gīśvara-gajāḥ"; a mnemonic for specific planetary alignments</note> that are beneficial for making these items.

Regarding the "Five-fold" period <term>Pañcaka</term> <note>A period of approximately five days when the Moon is in the signs of Aquarius and Pisces, specifically starting from the second half of the star Dhaniṣṭhā</note>: if one ignores this and performs the work—such as bringing in beds, couches, or collecting wood <note>original: "kāṣṭhādi saṃgraha"</note>—it leads to the suffering of the family or the onset of disease. This "Five-fold" restriction beginning with the star **Dhaniṣṭhā** <note>original: "dhaniṣṭhādi pañcake"</note> is a special rule that must be observed for all such domestic activities to ensure the well-being of the inhabitants.

### The Distinction of One’s Own Veda || 17 || This

Now, he describes the **installation of the deity in the temple** — When the knowledge of the scriptures is certain, one should place the deity in this temple<gloss>in the temple</gloss> according to the distinctions of one’s own tradition <term>Svāmnāya; the specific lineage of ritual transmission</term>. Through the distinction of one’s own Veda <insert>distinction</insert> and following the prescribed methods, one should perform the fire sacrifice rituals <term>Homa-karma</term>. At the time when the sacrifice is performed, one should invite Brahmins who are knowledgeable of the proper time <note>astrologically auspicious moments</note> and who are like elephants in their strength of learning, providing them with food and other necessities. Then, the protective ground is secured through the power of gifts. 43 Next, he describes the prowess of those who proceed in this way, using the example of Vikramarka <note>The legendary King Vikramaditya</note> in the land of Bharat <note>India</note>, by whom many temples were built:

> Through the fire sacrifice rituals spoken of in the various branches of one's own tradition, and through the giving of gifts and seats, one who has attained scriptural knowledge and understands the movement of time should gather the Brahmins and install the deities here. 43 That King Vikramarka shines upon the earth like a sovereign; he by whom many temples were built and presiding deities were established through Vedic regulations and the giving of gifts. 44 Thus ends the **seventeenth chapter on the installation of deities for entering a new home in the poem "The Delight of the Learned" composed by the Great Poet Kalidasa.**

<margin>Reference: Prapraruh</margin>
The temples were built by those skilled in the arts, and the presiding deities—the Lords of the Gods—were established and consecrated. That King Vikramarka shines as the lord of the earth. What kind of land is Bharat? It is where the "Shakas" <note>The Scythians or foreign invaders</note> have been removed. In the reading "Apashaka," it means the Shakas or barbarians <term>Mlechhas</term> are gone because he completed their destruction. Alternatively, it means the era of the Shakas was removed because he established his own era <note>referring to the Vikrama Samvat calendar era</note> after defeating them.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter on the sacrifice for the installation [of deities] when entering a new home in the "Universal Explanation" <term>Sarvabodhika; the title of the commentary</term>. || 17 ||

***

Now, he describes the **establishment of the sacred fire** <term>Agnyādhāna; the ritual of formally setting up the domestic sacrificial fires</term> at the time of marriage and other occasions. It is said that the **fourth rite** <note>original: caturthe karma; referring to the Caturthī-karma, a ritual performed on the fourth day after marriage</note> is for the purpose of establishing the fire on the seventh day of the wedding rituals.

This **time of taking a wife** <term>Sadārakāla</term>—otherwise known as the **marriage-time** <term>Vivāhakāla</term>—is declared as the first opportunity. Furthermore, it is said that for brothers who have wives, the **time of inheritance** <term>Dāyādakāla</term> occurs during the **division of property** <term>Dravyavibhāga</term>. In those instances—either at the time of marriage or at the time of inheritance—the **acceptance of the fire** <term>Agniparigraha</term> should take place for the fire establishment. Under what circumstances? While the **father** <note>original: janake pitari</note> or the **brother** is already maintaining and serving the fire in the home. 1. Now, concerning the brothers:

->The marriage-time is declared; between these two actions, the acceptance of the fire occurs there. The inheritance division involves the sharing of property among brothers.<-
->While the father is serving the fire, at that very moment, there is the acceptance of the sacrificial fire. During the time of the fire-establishment...<-
->...at the time of the junction (Sandhyā), for the sake of the success of the rite, according to the available opportunity, or due to the impossibility of the former...<-

<margin>He demonstrates the acceptance of the fire.</margin> In the words "at that time," he refers to this **marriage-time** <term>Sadārakāla</term> or **inheritance-time** <term>Dāyādakāla</term>; at that point, the acceptance of the fire should be performed from the father or the brother. At what specific time? At a time that is "shining and faultless" <note>original: babhruṇābhānti nirdoṣe</note>, meaning a time free of ritual defects and characterized by pure conduct. Furthermore, if that is impossible—perhaps because the father or elder brothers are not present—then the acceptance of the fire should be performed by the **performer of the union** <note>original: sandhātā; one who joins the ritual elements</note> at the first available and obtained opportunity to ensure the ritual's success.

# On the Auspicious Timings for the Acceptance of the Fire

Now, the auspicious planetary combinations for the **Acceptance of the Fire** <term>Agniparigraha; the ritual act of taking or establishing the sacred fire</term> are prescribed. On days other than the **"Empty" Lunar Days** <term>Rikta-tithi; the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar fortnight, considered hollow or inauspicious for new beginnings</term>, one seeks the adornment of satisfaction. The wise perform the **shaving of the beard** <term>Śmaśru-jādhanam; the ritual first cutting of hair/beard</term> and the **establishment of the fire** <note>original: ādhānam</note> during these times. At what specific times? On days that are not "Empty," avoiding the day of the **Son of the Sun** <note>original: Ravīsūnu; a name for the planet Saturn, thus meaning Saturday</note>, and avoiding the **Bharani** <note>original: Bhari</note> and **Vishakha** <note>original: Visha</note> constellations. These rites should be performed only in combinations that avoid these negative factors. Again, under what conditions? When there is **Lunar Strength** <term>Somavīrya; the auspicious strength and favorable position of the Moon</term>. 5.

Now, he explains the purification of the constellations for the **Acceptance of the Fire**. The **Masters** <note>original: Āryā Ācāryāḥ</note> describe the method for the **establishment of the new fire** <note>original: nayādhāna-vidhāna</note> as follows:

->On non-Empty days, avoiding Saturday, and the constellations of Bharani and Vishakha,<-
->the wise perform the shaving of the beard and the establishment of the fire<-
->with the adornment of satisfaction, while the Moon is strong. 5.<-
->In the growth-promoting constellations, and the three "Uttara" constellations,<-
->avoiding the influence of the malefic planets,<-
->is the method for the new establishment of the fire according to the Masters. 6.<-

The text praises the act of establishing the fire, explaining in which constellations it should occur. For the **Brahmins** <term>Viprāṇām; the priestly class</term>, he mentions the constellations governed by **Agni** <note>the Fire God, presiding over the Krittika constellation</note> and other lords. In which constellations specifically? In the dust <gloss>East</gloss> <note>original: reṇau; likely referring to the Eastern constellations or a specific subdivision</note> and those increasing in growth, such as **Krittika**. He further notes the influence of the **malefic planets** <term>Krūra-grahāṇām; literally "cruel planets" like Mars and Saturn</term> and their positions... 6.

"One should attain" <note>original: samīyāt</note> means one should obtain the "hand-fire" <note>karāgni</note>. # Regarding the Procedures

### The Threefold Seven Systems

Now begins the description of the year which is threefold in its seven systems. Having completed the placement of the fires, this is known through the forest deities <note>The "forest deities" likely refers to the natural spirits or cosmic powers that govern the timing of seasons and materials used in sacrifice</note> and understood by the foremost priests. Now, let those systems be described: first, the cooked-offering sacrifices <term>Paka-yajna; simple domestic rituals usually involving cooked grains or clarified butter</term>, which are sevenfold. Then, there are the seven systems of oblation-sacrifices <term>Havir-yajna; more complex rituals involving offerings like milk, curds, or medicinal plants into the fire</term>.

<margin>Agnihotra Sutra 2</margin>
These are specific ritual refinements. The Fire Offering <term>Agnihotra; the daily maintenance of the sacred fire at sunrise and sunset</term> is sevenfold, including the Full and New Moon sacrifices <term>Darshapurnamasa</term>. These are to be accomplished according to the time prescribed in the specific branch of the Vedas one follows. 

The seven systems of oblation-sacrifices <note>original: Havir-yajna samstha</note> are:
1. The introductory sacrifice <note>original: Pra-pravayaye</note>
2. The Full and New Moon sacrifices
3. The Four-Month seasonal sacrifices <term>Chaturmasyani</term>, specifically the All-Gods offering <note>original: Vaishvadeva</note>
4. The Varuna-Praghasa <note>offerings to the deity Varuna</note>
5. The Sakamedha <note>mid-seasonal offerings</note>
6. The Shunasiriya <note>offerings related to agriculture and the plow</note>
7. The Parva and Suvetha rituals
8. The Sautramani <note>a ritual to heal or strengthen the sacrificer</note>

As for the cooked-offering sacrifices <note>original: Paka-yajna</note>, which are also seven:
The Shravana rite, the Ashvayuji rite <note>performed on the full moon of the month of Ashvina</note>, the Agrahayani rite, the <insert>Anvashtaka</insert> rite, the Ashtaka rite <note>offerings to the ancestors on the eighth day after the full moon</note>, and the monthly Ashtaka.

Having established the dwelling place and being known by the deities of the ground, these must be accomplished at the times prescribed in the Vedas. Thus are the seven oblation-sacrifice systems described. The Ekashtaka <note>the eighth day of the dark half of the month of Magha</note> and the Ashtaka of the rainy season make up the cooked-offering systems. Then there are the seven Soma systems <term>Soma-samstha; major Vedic sacrifices involving the pressing and offering of the sacred Soma juice</term>, making fifteen major categories in total:
1. Agnistoma <note>the standard, most common Soma sacrifice</note>
2. Atyagnistoma
3. Ukthya
4. Shodashi
5. Atiratra
6. Vajapeya <note>the "Drink of Strength" ritual involving chariot races</note>

<margin>The end</margin>
7. Aptoryama. These are the seven Soma systems.

Now, in the context of the ritual residence, the measurement of the sacrificial altar <term>Vedi; a consecrated area of ground for ritual offerings</term> is written. It should be 32... three... and for the sake of the two horses (?) <note>The text here is highly technical, referring to specific geometric measurements for the altar</note> it is well-formed with five... twelve... and five and a half cubits <note>original: hasta</note>. This is the altar for the Full Moon sacrifice. Having measured and constructed the altar in this way, the procedure is described in the **Ritual Rule-book** <term>Sutra; a concise manual of ritual rules</term> **regarding the extension.** From that point, one releases the cord. At the point of six finger-widths <note>original: angula</note>, one should draw the opening <insert>at the front</insert> in the specified direction. On the side of the altar, the wooden stake <note>original: shanku</note> marks the measure of a cubit.

<term>Indra-Simha; literally "Indra-Lion," a title signifying a supreme ruler. Nara-chakra-trayam refers to three symbolic diagrams used in statecraft or ritual to represent different domains of power.</term>

# The Ritual Application of the Three Royal Wheels

Now, he demonstrates the "Wheel of the King’s Earth" <term>Rajamridvachakra; a ritual diagram or symbolic structure involving consecrated earth</term> as prescribed for sacrificial baths. It is said <gloss>A</gloss> that three circles must be constructed for both the <term>Avabhritha</term> <note>the final purificatory bath at the end of a Vedic sacrifice</note> and for the <term>Abhisheka</term> <note>the ceremonial anointment or coronation of a king</note>. 

In which contexts are these three circles proclaimed? <gloss>2</gloss> They are used for the **Virāt**, the **Samrāt**, and the **Rāṭ**. 

1. The **Virāt** <note>original: "virāji"; one who shines with particular distinction</note> is he who shines in a specific specialized manner. 
2. The **Samrāt** <note>one who shines universally or rules over other kings</note> is he who shines in a complete or perfect manner. 
3. The **Rāṭ** <note>short for Svarāt or Rati-rāt</note> is he who shines in his own delight or self-mastery. 

One should apply these circles in sequence. It should be understood that for the **Lord of Horses** <term>Ashvapati</term>, the circle takes the form of a **Lion**; for the **Lord of Elephants** <term>Gajapati</term>, it takes the form of a **Man**; and for the **Lord of Men** <term>Narapati</term>, it takes the form of a **Horse**. 

According to the traditions of the sacrifice:
The Brahmin who is the authorized performer of the <term>Agnihotra</term> <note>the daily fire-offering</note> is proclaimed as a **Rāṭ**. 
Through the performance of the <term>Vajapeya</term> sacrifice <note>the "Drink of Strength," a high-status ritual</note>, one is known as a **Samrāt**. 
The **Virāt** is distinguished through his specific sacrificial standing.

# Concerning the Lion-Throne and the Lord of the World

When the Lord of the World <note>original: "Lokeshaka"; refers to the King or a presiding deity</note> is seated upon the **Lion-Throne**, the King becomes like the planet Mars <note>original: "Angarakara"; the red planet associated with power and war</note> in strength. Before him, the King shines as the <gloss>nectar-giving</gloss> **Moon**. In this matter, if the planet is single-mindedly focused on the "House of the Son" <note>the 5th astrological house, governing wisdom and offspring</term>, and stays there even as time passes, the King receives the merit of the **Consecration** <term>Abhisheka; the ritual bathing and crowning of a monarch</term>. 25.

Now, he describes the unfavorable results of a **Malefic Planet** <term>Papagraha; planets like Mars or Saturn that are thought to bring challenges</term> in this context. Regarding the "Auspicious Seat" <note>original: "Bhadrasana"; a specific ceremonial chair</note>: if a malefic planet is positioned to the left at the time of the Consecration, or if the Consecration is joined by a malefic planet, the King or his city will fall into ruin.

---

### The Power of the Enthronement Circle

When the Lord of the World is established on the **Throne**, and the "House of Wisdom" is not afflicted, he attains the fruit of that time through the **Consecration**, dwelling in happiness like one in a celestial garden. 25.
If a **Malefic Planet** moves to the left of the **Auspicious Seat** during the Consecration, the King and his city will be destroyed. If a malefic planet is present, the city is left empty and the King is lost. 26.
The circle known as the **Lion-Throne** <note>original: "Simhasanakhya-valayam"</note> is truly beautiful; its power is supreme in the matter of the King's Consecration. This is famous and should not be otherwise, despite any contradictions found between the **Jaina Scriptures** <note>original: "Jainagama"</note> and **Vedic Rituals** <note>original: "Nigama-karma"</note>.
